translations.chinese: 卷五十二 竇田灌韓傳第二十二
translations.literal: Volume 52: Biographies of Dou, Tian, Guan, and Han, number twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 52: Biographies of Dou, Tian, Guan, and Han (Part 22).

translations.chinese: 竇嬰字王孫，孝文皇后從兄子也。
translations.literal: Dou Ying, courtesy name Wangsun, was the son of a cousin of Empress Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying, whose courtesy name was Wangsun, was a nephew of Empress Xiaowen.

context.next: 父世觀津人也。

translations.chinese: 父世觀津人也。
translations.literal: His father's family for generations were people of Guanjin.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his father's people had hailed from Guanjin.

context.previous: 竇嬰字王孫，孝文皇后從兄子也。
context.next: 喜賓客。

translations.chinese: 喜賓客。
translations.literal: He delighted in guests.
translations.idiomatic: He loved entertaining guests.

context.previous: 父世觀津人也。
context.next: 孝文時為吳相，病免。

translations.chinese: 孝文時為吳相，病免。
translations.literal: Under Emperor Wen he was chancellor of Wu; he was dismissed because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wen's reign he served as chancellor of Wu, then stepped down citing illness.

context.previous: 喜賓客。
context.next: 孝景即位，為詹事。

translations.chinese: 孝景即位，為詹事。
translations.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he became chamberlain for the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing took the throne, Dou Ying was appointed chamberlain for the heir apparent.

context.previous: 孝文時為吳相，病免。

translations.chinese: 帝弟梁孝王，母竇太后愛之。
translations.literal: The emperor's younger brother, King Xiao of Liang, his mother Empress Dowager Dou loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's younger brother, King Xiao of Liang, was the favorite of his mother, Empress Dowager Dou.

context.next: 孝王朝，因燕昆弟飲。

translations.chinese: 孝王朝，因燕昆弟飲。
translations.literal: When King Xiao attended court, he joined in drinking with the emperor and their cousins as kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Liang came to court, he drank with the emperor and their cousins as family.

context.previous: 帝弟梁孝王，母竇太后愛之。
context.next: 是時，上未立太子，酒酣，上從容曰：「千秋萬歲後傳王。」

translations.chinese: 是時，上未立太子，酒酣，上從容曰：「千秋萬歲後傳王。」
translations.literal: At that time the emperor had not yet established an heir apparent; when the wine was deep, the emperor said at ease, "After a thousand autumns and ten thousand years I will pass the throne to you, my prince."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet named an heir; when the wine had gone round, he said lightly, "When I am gone, I mean to leave the realm to you."

context.previous: 孝王朝，因燕昆弟飲。
context.next: 太后歡。

translations.chinese: 太后歡。
translations.literal: The empress dowager was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was delighted.

context.previous: 是時，上未立太子，酒酣，上從容曰：「千秋萬歲後傳王。」
context.next: 嬰引卮酒進上曰：「天下者，高祖天下，父子相傳，漢之約也，上何以得傳梁王！」

translations.chinese: 嬰引卮酒進上曰：「天下者，高祖天下，父子相傳，漢之約也，上何以得傳梁王！」
translations.literal: Ying raised a cup of wine, advanced it to the emperor, and said, "The empire is the empire of Gaozu; father and son pass it to one another—this is the covenant of Han. How can Your Majesty pass it to the King of Liang!"
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying lifted his cup, offered it to the emperor, and said, "The realm belongs to Gaozu's line; fathers pass it to sons—that is Han's compact. How could you hand it to the king of Liang?"

context.previous: 太后歡。
context.next: 太后由此憎嬰。

translations.chinese: 太后由此憎嬰。
translations.literal: From this the empress dowager hated Ying.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the empress dowager bore him a grudge.

context.previous: 嬰引卮酒進上曰：「天下者，高祖天下，父子相傳，漢之約也，上何以得傳梁王！」
context.next: 嬰亦薄其官，因病免。

translations.chinese: 嬰亦薄其官，因病免。
translations.literal: Ying also thought little of his office; because of illness he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying came to despise his post as well and resigned, pleading illness.

context.previous: 太后由此憎嬰。
context.next: 太后除嬰門籍，不得朝請。

translations.chinese: 太后除嬰門籍，不得朝請。
translations.literal: The empress dowager removed Ying from the gate register; he was not permitted court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: She struck his name from the palace gate list, barring him from the morning and evening audiences.

context.previous: 嬰亦薄其官，因病免。

translations.chinese: 孝景三年，吳、楚反、上察宗室諸竇無如嬰賢，召入見，固讓謝，稱病不足任。
translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Jing, Wu and Chu rebelled. The emperor surveyed the imperial Dou clan and found none as worthy as Ying; he summoned him for an audience. Ying firmly declined and apologized, saying he was ill and unfit for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's third year, Wu and Chu rose in revolt. The emperor looked over the Dou kinsmen and found no one worthier than Dou Ying, so he summoned him. Dou Ying refused again and again, apologizing and insisting he was too ill to serve.

context.next: 太后亦慚。

translations.chinese: 太后亦慚。
translations.literal: The empress dowager was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was abashed.

context.previous: 孝景三年，吳、楚反、上察宗室諸竇無如嬰賢，召入見，固讓謝，稱病不足任。
context.next: 於是上曰：「天下方有急，王孫寧可以讓邪？」

translations.chinese: 於是上曰：「天下方有急，王孫寧可以讓邪？」
translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor said, "The realm is in crisis; can Wangsun decline?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The empire is in peril—can Wangsun still refuse?"

context.previous: 太后亦慚。
context.next: 乃拜嬰為大將軍，賜金千斤。

translations.chinese: 乃拜嬰為大將軍，賜金千斤。
translations.literal: Then he appointed Ying grand marshal and bestowed a thousand catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Dou Ying grand marshal and gave him a thousand catties of gold.

context.previous: 於是上曰：「天下方有急，王孫寧可以讓邪？」
context.next: 嬰言爰盎、欒布諸名將賢士在家者進之。

translations.chinese: 嬰言爰盎、欒布諸名將賢士在家者進之。
translations.literal: Ying spoke of Yuan Ang, Luan Bu, and other famous generals and worthy scholars at home and advanced them.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying recommended Yuan Ang, Luan Bu, and other noted generals and scholars then living in retirement.

context.previous: 乃拜嬰為大將軍，賜金千斤。
context.next: 所賜金，陳廊廡下，軍吏過，輒令財取為用，金無入家者。

translations.chinese: 所賜金，陳廊廡下，軍吏過，輒令財取為用，金無入家者。
translations.literal: The gold he was given he spread beneath the corridors and wings; when army clerks passed, he always told them to take what they needed for expenses; none of the gold entered his household.
translations.idiomatic: He piled the gifted gold in his corridors and told any passing clerk to help himself; none of it went into his private coffers.

context.previous: 嬰言爰盎、欒布諸名將賢士在家者進之。
context.next: 嬰守滎陽，監齊、趙兵。

translations.chinese: 嬰守滎陽，監齊、趙兵。
translations.literal: Ying held Yingyang and supervised the troops of Qi and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He held Yingyang and oversaw the Qi and Zhao forces.

context.previous: 所賜金，陳廊廡下，軍吏過，輒令財取為用，金無入家者。
context.next: 七國破，封為魏其侯。

translations.chinese: 七國破，封為魏其侯。
translations.literal: When the seven states were defeated, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: After the seven kingdoms were crushed, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Weiqi.

context.previous: 嬰守滎陽，監齊、趙兵。
context.next: 游士賓客爭歸之。

translations.chinese: 游士賓客爭歸之。
translations.literal: Wandering scholars and guests vied to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Roving scholars and clients flocked to his door.

context.previous: 七國破，封為魏其侯。
context.next: 每朝議大事，條侯、魏其，列侯莫敢與亢禮。

translations.chinese: 每朝議大事，條侯、魏其，列侯莫敢與亢禮。
translations.literal: Whenever the court debated great matters, Marquis of Tiao and Marquis of Weiqi stood so high that none of the other marquises dared match them in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At every weighty court debate, Marquis Zhou Yafu and Marquis Dou Ying were preeminent—no other marquis dared claim equal precedence with them.

context.previous: 游士賓客爭歸之。

translations.chinese: 四年，立栗太子，以嬰為傅。
translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Li heir apparent was established, and Ying was made his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the heir from the Li family was installed, with Dou Ying as his tutor.

context.next: 七年，栗太子廢，嬰爭弗能得，謝病，屏居藍田南山下數月，諸竇賓客辯士說，莫能來。

translations.chinese: 七年，栗太子廢，嬰爭弗能得，謝病，屏居藍田南山下數月，諸竇賓客辯士說，莫能來。
translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Li heir apparent was deposed. Ying remonstrated but could not prevail; he pleaded illness, withdrew, and lived in seclusion for several months at the foot of Mount Lan in Lantian. Dou kinsmen, guests, and debaters urged him, but none could bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year that heir was cast aside. Dou Ying argued in vain, then pleaded illness and shut himself away for months below Blue Field Mountain. Kinsmen, clients, and rhetoricians tried to coax him out; none succeeded.

context.previous: 四年，立栗太子，以嬰為傅。
context.next: 梁人高遂乃說嬰曰：「能富貴將軍者，上也；

translations.chinese: 梁人高遂乃說嬰曰：「能富貴將軍者，上也；
translations.literal: Gao Sui of Liang then said to Ying, "The one who can enrich and ennoble the general is the throne;"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sui of Liang told him, "Only the emperor can make you rich and exalted;"

context.previous: 七年，栗太子廢，嬰爭弗能得，謝病，屏居藍田南山下數月，諸竇賓客辯士說，莫能來。
context.next: 能親將軍者，太后也。

translations.chinese: 能親將軍者，太后也。
translations.literal: and the one who can draw the general close is the empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: and only the empress dowager can keep you in favor."

context.previous: 梁人高遂乃說嬰曰：「能富貴將軍者，上也；
context.next: 今將軍傅太子，太子廢，爭不能拔，又不能死，自引謝病，擁趙女屏閒處而不朝，只加懟自明，揚主之過。

translations.chinese: 今將軍傅太子，太子廢，爭不能拔，又不能死，自引謝病，擁趙女屏閒處而不朝，只加懟自明，揚主之過。
translations.literal: "Now the general tutored the heir apparent; when he was deposed, you could not save him nor die for the cause. You excused yourself on illness, keep Zhao women in your inner chambers and do not attend court—this only adds resentment, tries to clear yourself, and advertises the ruler's faults."
translations.idiomatic: "You tutored the crown prince; when he fell, you could neither reverse it nor die with honor. You hide behind illness, fill your inner rooms with Zhao women, and shun court—only inviting blame and parading the sovereign's errors before the world."

context.previous: 能親將軍者，太后也。
context.next: 有如兩宮奭將軍，則妻子無類矣。」

translations.chinese: 有如兩宮奭將軍，則妻子無類矣。」
translations.literal: "Should the two palaces turn on you, General, your wife and children will leave no posterity."
translations.idiomatic: "If emperor and dowager both turn on you, your family will not survive."

context.previous: 今將軍傅太子，太子廢，爭不能拔，又不能死，自引謝病，擁趙女屏閒處而不朝，只加懟自明，揚主之過。
context.next: 嬰然之，乃起，朝請如故。

translations.chinese: 嬰然之，乃起，朝請如故。
translations.literal: Ying agreed with this; then he rose and attended court as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying saw the force of it, rose, and resumed his court duties.

context.previous: 有如兩宮奭將軍，則妻子無類矣。」

translations.chinese: 桃侯免相，竇太后數言魏其。
translations.literal: When Marquis of Tao was dismissed as chancellor, Empress Dowager Dou repeatedly spoke of Marquis of Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: After Marquis of Tao left the chancellorship, Empress Dowager Dou kept pressing Dou Ying's name.

context.next: 景帝曰：「太后豈以臣有愛相魏其者？

translations.chinese: 景帝曰：「太后豈以臣有愛相魏其者？
translations.literal: Emperor Jing said, "Surely the empress dowager does not think I have some partiality and would make Marquis of Weiqi chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing replied, "Does my mother imagine I favor Dou Ying so much that I would make him chancellor?"

context.previous: 桃侯免相，竇太后數言魏其。
context.next: 魏其沾沾自喜耳，多易，難以為相持重。」

translations.chinese: 魏其沾沾自喜耳，多易，難以為相持重。」
translations.literal: "Marquis of Weiqi is smug and self-satisfied, reckless in many things, and difficult to make chancellor with the gravity it requires."
translations.idiomatic: "He is pleased with himself, flighty, and unfit to bear the weight of the chancellorship."

context.previous: 景帝曰：「太后豈以臣有愛相魏其者？
context.next: 遂不用，用建陵侯衛綰為丞相。

translations.chinese: 遂不用，用建陵侯衛綰為丞相。
translations.literal: So he was not used; Jianling Marquis Wei Wan was appointed chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: So Dou Ying was passed over, and Jianling Marquis Wei Wan became chancellor.

context.previous: 魏其沾沾自喜耳，多易，難以為相持重。」

translations.chinese: 田蚡，孝景王皇后同母弟也，生長陵。
translations.literal: Tian Fen was the uterine younger brother of Empress Wang of Emperor Jing; he was born and grew up in Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen was Empress Wang's full brother—Emperor Jing's empress—and had grown up in Changling.

context.next: 竇嬰已為大將軍，方盛，蚡為諸曹郎，未貴，往來侍酒嬰所，跪起如子姓。

translations.chinese: 竇嬰已為大將軍，方盛，蚡為諸曹郎，未貴，往來侍酒嬰所，跪起如子姓。
translations.literal: When Dou Ying had already become grand marshal and was flourishing, Fen was a gentleman of the various bureaus, not yet eminent; he would come and go to wait upon Ying at his wine parties, kneeling and rising like a son or nephew.
translations.idiomatic: While Dou Ying stood at the head of the armies, Tian Fen was still a petty bureau clerk; he waited on Dou Ying at his feasts, kneeling and rising like a junior kinsman.

context.previous: 田蚡，孝景王皇后同母弟也，生長陵。
context.next: 及孝景晚節，蚡益貴幸，為中大夫。

translations.chinese: 及孝景晚節，蚡益貴幸，為中大夫。
translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Jing, Fen grew ever more honored and favored, and became palace counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Jing's reign Tian Fen rose in favor until he held the post of palace counselor.

context.previous: 竇嬰已為大將軍，方盛，蚡為諸曹郎，未貴，往來侍酒嬰所，跪起如子姓。
context.next: 辯有口，學《盤盂》諸書，王皇后賢之。

translations.chinese: 辯有口，學《盤盂》諸書，王皇后賢之。
translations.literal: He was eloquent and quick of tongue, studied the texts in the "Bowl and Basin" series, and Empress Wang thought him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He was a sharp debater, had read the ritual compendiums such as the Pan Yu texts, and Empress Wang judged him capable.

context.previous: 及孝景晚節，蚡益貴幸，為中大夫。

translations.chinese: 孝景崩，武帝初即位，蚡以舅封為武安侯，弟勝為周陽侯。
translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu first mounted the throne, Fen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an for being the maternal uncle; his younger brother Sheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhouyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu took the throne, Tian Fen was made marquis of Wu'an as the emperor's uncle; his brother Tian Sheng became marquis of Zhouyang.

context.next: 蚡新用事，卑下賓客，進名士家居者貴之，欲以傾諸將相。

translations.chinese: 蚡新用事，卑下賓客，進名士家居者貴之，欲以傾諸將相。
translations.literal: Fen had newly come to power; he humbled himself before guests and advanced scholars of repute at home to honor them, intending thereby to overturn the generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Newly in power, he played humble host and elevated famous scholars in retirement, aiming to eclipse the established generals and ministers.

context.previous: 孝景崩，武帝初即位，蚡以舅封為武安侯，弟勝為周陽侯。
context.next: 上所填撫，多蚡賓客計策。

translations.chinese: 上所填撫，多蚡賓客計策。
translations.literal: Much of what the emperor settled and pacified followed the plans of Fen's guests.
translations.idiomatic: Much of what the emperor decided followed advice from Tian Fen's clients.

context.previous: 蚡新用事，卑下賓客，進名士家居者貴之，欲以傾諸將相。
context.next: 會丞相綰病免，上議置丞相、太尉。

translations.chinese: 會丞相綰病免，上議置丞相、太尉。
translations.literal: When it happened that Chancellor Wan fell ill and resigned, the court discussed appointing a chancellor and grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Wei Wan fell ill and stepped down, the court debated who should fill the chancellorship and grand commandancy.

context.previous: 上所填撫，多蚡賓客計策。
context.next: 藉福說蚡曰：「魏其侯貴久矣，素天下士歸之。

translations.chinese: 藉福說蚡曰：「魏其侯貴久矣，素天下士歸之。
translations.literal: Jifu said to Fen, "Marquis of Weiqi has long been noble; men of talent across the realm have always turned to him."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu warned Tian Fen, "Marquis Dou has been exalted for years; the empire's best men already follow him."

context.previous: 會丞相綰病免，上議置丞相、太尉。
context.next: 今將軍初興，未如，即上以將軍為相，必讓魏其。

translations.chinese: 今將軍初興，未如，即上以將軍為相，必讓魏其。
translations.literal: "Now the general has only just risen; you are not his equal. If the throne makes the general chancellor at once, you are bound to yield to Marquis of Weiqi."
translations.idiomatic: "You are only just rising; you cannot match him. If the throne names you chancellor now, you will have to defer to Dou Ying."

context.previous: 藉福說蚡曰：「魏其侯貴久矣，素天下士歸之。
context.next: 魏其為相，將軍必為太尉。

translations.chinese: 魏其為相，將軍必為太尉。
translations.literal: "When Marquis of Weiqi is chancellor, the general is sure to become grand commandant."
translations.idiomatic: "Let Dou Ying take the chancellorship, and you may still win the grand commandancy."

context.previous: 今將軍初興，未如，即上以將軍為相，必讓魏其。
context.next: 太尉、相尊等耳，有讓賢名。」

translations.chinese: 太尉、相尊等耳，有讓賢名。」
translations.literal: "Grand commandant and chancellor are of equal dignity; you will have a name for yielding worthily to another."
translations.idiomatic: "Those two posts are peers in rank—and you gain a reputation for yielding to the worthier man."

context.previous: 魏其為相，將軍必為太尉。
context.next: 蚡乃微言太后風上，於是乃以嬰為丞相，蚡為太尉。

translations.chinese: 蚡乃微言太后風上，於是乃以嬰為丞相，蚡為太尉。
translations.literal: Fen then dropped subtle words to the empress dowager so that she might influence the emperor; accordingly Ying was made chancellor and Fen grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen whispered as much to his sister the empress dowager, who swayed the emperor; Dou Ying became chancellor and Tian Fen grand commandant.

context.previous: 太尉、相尊等耳，有讓賢名。」
context.next: 藉福賀嬰，因吊曰：「君侯資性喜善疾惡，方今善人譽君侯，故至丞相；

translations.chinese: 藉福賀嬰，因吊曰：「君侯資性喜善疾惡，方今善人譽君侯，故至丞相；
translations.literal: Jifu congratulated Ying but then offered condolences, saying, "By nature you delight in good men and hate evil. Now good men praise you, my lord, and therefore you have reached the chancellorship;"
translations.idiomatic: Jifu congratulated Dou Ying, then mourned his fate: "You love the good and hate the wicked; the good have lifted you to the chancellorship;"

context.previous: 蚡乃微言太后風上，於是乃以嬰為丞相，蚡為太尉。
context.next: 然惡人眾，亦且毀君侯。

translations.chinese: 然惡人眾，亦且毀君侯。
translations.literal: "yet evil men are many, and they will also slander you, my lord."
translations.idiomatic: "but the wicked are legion, and they will tear you down."

context.previous: 藉福賀嬰，因吊曰：「君侯資性喜善疾惡，方今善人譽君侯，故至丞相；
context.next: 君侯能兼容，則幸久；

translations.chinese: 君侯能兼容，則幸久；
translations.literal: "If you can tolerate both sides, you may long remain fortunate;"
translations.idiomatic: "If you can stomach both camps, you may endure;"

context.previous: 然惡人眾，亦且毀君侯。
context.next: 不能，今以毀去矣。」

translations.chinese: 不能，今以毀去矣。」
translations.literal: "if you cannot, you will now be ruined by slander and cast out."
translations.idiomatic: "if not, slander will drive you out at once."

context.previous: 君侯能兼容，則幸久；
context.next: 嬰不聽。

translations.chinese: 嬰不聽。
translations.literal: Ying would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying paid no heed.

context.previous: 不能，今以毀去矣。」

translations.chinese: 嬰、蚡俱好儒術，推轂趙綰為御史大夫，王臧為郎中令。
translations.literal: Ying and Fen both favored Confucian learning; they recommended Zhao Wan as censor-in-chief and Wang Zang as supervisor of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Both men favored Confucian policy; they secured Zhao Wan as censor-in-chief and Wang Zang as supervisor of the imperial household.

context.next: 迎魯申公，欲設明堂，令列侯就國，除關，以禮為服制，以興太平。

translations.chinese: 迎魯申公，欲設明堂，令列侯就國，除關，以禮為服制，以興太平。
translations.literal: They welcomed the Duke of Shen from Lu, wished to establish the Bright Hall, ordered the marquises to take up their fiefs in the states, abolished the passes, and intended to regulate mourning garments by ritual so as to bring about great peace.
translations.idiomatic: They brought in the Duke of Shen from Lu, planned a Bright Hall, ordered nobles back to their fiefs, lifted internal customs barriers, and meant to reform dress and ritual for an age of peace.

context.previous: 嬰、蚡俱好儒術，推轂趙綰為御史大夫，王臧為郎中令。
context.next: 舉謫諸竇宗室無行者，除其屬籍。

translations.chinese: 舉謫諸竇宗室無行者，除其屬籍。
translations.literal: They denounced various Dou kin of the imperial house who lacked conduct and removed their names from the clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: They impeached dissolute Dou relatives of the throne and struck them from the imperial genealogy.

context.previous: 迎魯申公，欲設明堂，令列侯就國，除關，以禮為服制，以興太平。
context.next: 諸外家為列侯，列侯多尚公主，皆不欲就國，以故毀日至竇太后。

translations.chinese: 諸外家為列侯，列侯多尚公主，皆不欲就國，以故毀日至竇太后。
translations.literal: The various maternal families who were marquises—marquises for the most part had married princesses—all wished not to go to their fiefs; for this reason slander poured in daily to Empress Dowager Dou.
translations.idiomatic: The consort families who held marquisates—most of those lords had married princesses—refused to leave the capital; daily slander reached Empress Dowager Dou.

context.previous: 舉謫諸竇宗室無行者，除其屬籍。
context.next: 太后好黃、老言，而嬰、蚡、趙綰等務隆推儒術，貶道家言，是以竇太后滋不說。

translations.chinese: 太后好黃、老言，而嬰、蚡、趙綰等務隆推儒術，貶道家言，是以竇太后滋不說。
translations.literal: The empress dowager favored Huang-Lao teachings, while Ying, Fen, and Zhao Wan strove to exalt Confucian learning and depreciate Daoist discourse, so Empress Dowager Dou grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: She was devoted to Huang-Lao quietism, while Dou Ying, Tian Fen, and Zhao Wan pushed Confucian orthodoxy and slighted Daoist lore—so her dislike deepened.

context.previous: 諸外家為列侯，列侯多尚公主，皆不欲就國，以故毀日至竇太后。

translations.chinese: 二年，御史大夫趙綰請毋奏事東宮。
translations.literal: In the second year, Censor-in-chief Zhao Wan requested that memorials no longer be submitted to the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhao Wan asked that state papers no longer be routed through the eastern palace—the empress dowager's residence.

context.next: 竇太后大怒，曰：「此欲復為新垣平邪！」

translations.chinese: 竇太后大怒，曰：「此欲復為新垣平邪！」
translations.literal: Empress Dowager Dou flew into a rage and said, "Is this not an attempt to play Xin Yuanping again!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Dou exploded: "So you mean to play Xin Yuanping again!"

context.previous: 二年，御史大夫趙綰請毋奏事東宮。
context.next: 乃罷逐趙綰、王臧，而免丞相嬰、太尉蚡，以柏至侯許昌為丞相，武強侯莊青翟為御史大夫。

translations.chinese: 乃罷逐趙綰、王臧，而免丞相嬰、太尉蚡，以柏至侯許昌為丞相，武強侯莊青翟為御史大夫。
translations.literal: Thereupon she dismissed and expelled Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, removed Chancellor Ying and Grand Commandant Fen from office, appointed Marquis of Bozhi Xu Chang as chancellor, and Marquis of Wuqiang Zhuang Qingdi as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: She drove out Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, stripped Dou Ying and Tian Fen of their posts, named Marquis of Bozhi Xu Chang chancellor, and Marquis of Wuqiang Zhuang Qingdi censor-in-chief.

context.previous: 竇太后大怒，曰：「此欲復為新垣平邪！」
context.next: 嬰、蚡以侯家居。

translations.chinese: 嬰、蚡以侯家居。
translations.literal: Ying and Fen lived at home holding only their marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying and Tian Fen retired to private life, marquises in name only.

context.previous: 乃罷逐趙綰、王臧，而免丞相嬰、太尉蚡，以柏至侯許昌為丞相，武強侯莊青翟為御史大夫。
context.next: 蚡雖不任職，以王太后故親幸，數言事，多效，士吏趨勢利者皆去嬰而歸蚡。

translations.chinese: 蚡雖不任職，以王太后故親幸，數言事，多效，士吏趨勢利者皆去嬰而歸蚡。
translations.literal: Although Fen held no office, he remained close and favored because of Empress Dowager Wang; he spoke frequently on policy and was often heeded. Officials and scholars who ran after gain left Ying and attached themselves to Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tian Fen had no title, Empress Dowager Wang kept him at the emperor's ear; his counsel usually prevailed, and every careerist deserted Dou Ying for him.

context.previous: 嬰、蚡以侯家居。
context.next: 蚡日益橫。

translations.chinese: 蚡日益橫。
translations.literal: Fen grew ever more overbearing by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day Tian Fen grew more arrogant.

context.previous: 蚡雖不任職，以王太后故親幸，數言事，多效，士吏趨勢利者皆去嬰而歸蚡。

translations.chinese: 六年，竇太后崩，丞相昌、御史大夫青翟坐喪事不辦，免。
translations.literal: In the sixth year, Empress Dowager Dou died; Chancellor Chang and Censor-in-chief Qingdi were dismissed because the funeral arrangements had not been handled properly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Empress Dowager Dou died; Chancellor Xu Chang and Censor-in-chief Zhuang Qingdi lost their posts over mishandled funeral duties.

context.next: 上以蚡為丞相，大司農韓安國為御史大夫。

translations.chinese: 上以蚡為丞相，大司農韓安國為御史大夫。
translations.literal: The emperor appointed Fen chancellor and Minister of Finance Han Anguo censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Tian Fen chancellor and Minister of Finance Han Anguo censor-in-chief.

context.previous: 六年，竇太后崩，丞相昌、御史大夫青翟坐喪事不辦，免。
context.next: 天下士郡諸侯愈益附蚡。

translations.chinese: 天下士郡諸侯愈益附蚡。
translations.literal: Men of talent under the commanderies and marquises leaned toward Fen all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and nobles across the commanderies flocked to him in greater numbers.

context.previous: 上以蚡為丞相，大司農韓安國為御史大夫。

translations.chinese: 蚡為人貌侵，生貴甚。
translations.literal: Fen was personally unprepossessing in appearance yet had been born to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen was homely in face but born to privilege.

context.next: 又以為諸侯王多長，上初即位，富於春秋，蚡以肺附為相，非痛折節以禮屈之，天下不肅。

translations.chinese: 又以為諸侯王多長，上初即位，富於春秋，蚡以肺附為相，非痛折節以禮屈之，天下不肅。
translations.literal: He also believed that many of the imperial princes were senior in years while the emperor had only just ascended the throne and was still young in years; Fen as chancellor by virtue of being kin to the throne, unless he bent them harshly with ritual, the realm would not stand in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the feudal kings grown old and proud while the young emperor still lacked years on the throne; as a kinsman-chancellor, he thought, he must break their pride with ritual or the realm would not fear him.

context.previous: 蚡為人貌侵，生貴甚。
context.next: 當是時，丞相入奏事，語移日，所言皆聽。

translations.chinese: 當是時，丞相入奏事，語移日，所言皆聽。
translations.literal: At that time, when the chancellor entered to memorialize, his discourse would last a whole day, and whatever he said was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he went in to report, he could talk the whole day through—and the throne accepted nearly every word.

context.previous: 又以為諸侯王多長，上初即位，富於春秋，蚡以肺附為相，非痛折節以禮屈之，天下不肅。
context.next: 薦人或起家至二千石，權移主上。

translations.chinese: 薦人或起家至二千石，權移主上。
translations.literal: When he recommended someone, the man might rise from commoner to rank at two thousand piculs; authority slipped from the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A man he sponsored might leap from commoner to two-thousand-picul rank in one step; power drained from the emperor into his hands.

context.previous: 當是時，丞相入奏事，語移日，所言皆聽。
context.next: 上乃曰：「君除吏盡未？

translations.chinese: 上乃曰：「君除吏盡未？
translations.literal: The emperor then said, "Have you, sir, finished appointing all your officials?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally asked, "Are you done handing out offices?"

context.previous: 薦人或起家至二千石，權移主上。
context.next: 吾亦欲除吏。」

translations.chinese: 吾亦欲除吏。」
translations.literal: "I too wish to appoint officials."
translations.idiomatic: "I still have a few appointments of my own to make."

context.previous: 上乃曰：「君除吏盡未？
context.next: 嘗請考工地益宅，上怒曰：「遂取武庫！」

translations.chinese: 嘗請考工地益宅，上怒曰：「遂取武庫！」
translations.literal: He once requested land from the Directorate of Works for his residence; the emperor angrily said, "Why not take the armory as well!"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked the Directorate of Works for more ground for his mansion; the emperor snapped, "Why not annex the imperial armory while you are at it?"

context.previous: 吾亦欲除吏。」
context.next: 是後乃退。

translations.chinese: 是後乃退。
translations.literal: After that he drew back.
translations.idiomatic: After that he pulled in his horns.

context.previous: 嘗請考工地益宅，上怒曰：「遂取武庫！」
context.next: 召客飲，坐其兄蓋侯北鄉，自坐東鄉，以為漢相尊，不可以兄故私橈。

translations.chinese: 召客飲，坐其兄蓋侯北鄉，自坐東鄉，以為漢相尊，不可以兄故私橈。
translations.literal: When he called guests to drink, he seated his elder brother Marquis of Gai with his mat facing north while he himself sat facing east, holding that the Han chancellor's dignity could not be bent for private reasons on account of an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: At feasts he gave his elder brother, Marquis of Gai, the inferior north-facing seat while he took the host's east, insisting that the chancellor of Han could not bend rank for kinship.

context.previous: 是後乃退。
context.next: 由此滋驕，治宅甲諸第，田園極膏腴，市買郡縣器物相屬於道。

translations.chinese: 由此滋驕，治宅甲諸第，田園極膏腴，市買郡縣器物相屬於道。
translations.literal: From this he grew only more arrogant; he built a residence that outshone all others, his fields and gardens were the richest, and purchasers from commanderies and counties convoyed goods along the roads without end.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance only swelled: his house outshone every peer's, his farms were the richest in the land, and wagons from distant counties lined the roads with gifts.

context.previous: 召客飲，坐其兄蓋侯北鄉，自坐東鄉，以為漢相尊，不可以兄故私橈。
context.next: 前堂羅鐘鼓，立曲旃；

translations.chinese: 前堂羅鐘鼓，立曲旃；
translations.literal: In his front hall he arrayed bells and drums and raised curved banners;
translations.idiomatic: His front hall rang with bells and drums and flew curved banners;

context.previous: 由此滋驕，治宅甲諸第，田園極膏腴，市買郡縣器物相屬於道。
context.next: 後房婦女以百數。

translations.chinese: 後房婦女以百數。
translations.literal: his rear chambers held womenfolk by the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: his inner quarters housed hundreds of women.

context.previous: 前堂羅鐘鼓，立曲旃；
context.next: 諸奏珍物狗馬玩好，不可勝數。

translations.chinese: 諸奏珍物狗馬玩好，不可勝數。
translations.literal: The rare treasures, dogs, horses, and curios presented to him could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Rare curios, hounds, and horses arrived in numbers beyond counting.

context.previous: 後房婦女以百數。

translations.chinese: 而嬰失竇太后，益疏不用，無勢，諸公稍自引而怠驁，唯灌夫獨否。
translations.literal: Meanwhile Ying had lost Empress Dowager Dou's support, was ever more estranged and unused, and had no power; eminent men gradually withdrew and treated him with neglect, but Guan Fu alone did not.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying, cut off after Empress Dowager Dou's death, was left idle and powerless; grandees drifted away and snubbed him—only Guan Fu stood by him.

context.next: 故嬰墨墨不得意，而厚遇夫也。

translations.chinese: 故嬰墨墨不得意，而厚遇夫也。
translations.literal: Therefore Ying was depressed and discontented, yet treated Fu generously.
translations.idiomatic: Brooding and embittered, Dou Ying lavished kindness on Guan Fu nonetheless.

context.previous: 而嬰失竇太后，益疏不用，無勢，諸公稍自引而怠驁，唯灌夫獨否。

translations.chinese: 灌夫字仲孺，穎陰人也。
translations.literal: Guan Fu, courtesy name Zhongru, was a man of Yingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu, courtesy name Zhongru, came from Yingyin.

context.next: 父張孟，嘗為穎陰侯灌嬰舍人，得幸，因進之，至二千石，故蒙灌氏姓為灌孟。

translations.chinese: 父張孟，嘗為穎陰侯灌嬰舍人，得幸，因進之，至二千石，故蒙灌氏姓為灌孟。
translations.literal: His father Zhang Meng had once been a retainer to Marquis of Yingyin Guan Ying, won favor, and was promoted through him to two thousand piculs; for this reason he took the Guan surname and was known as Guan Meng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Meng had been a client of Marquis Guan Ying of Yingyin, won promotion through him to two-thousand-picul rank, and adopted the Guan clan name as Guan Meng.

context.previous: 灌夫字仲孺，穎陰人也。
context.next: 吳、楚反時，穎陰侯灌嬰為將軍，屬太尉，請孟為校尉。

translations.chinese: 吳、楚反時，穎陰侯灌嬰為將軍，屬太尉，請孟為校尉。
translations.literal: During the rebellion of Wu and Chu, Marquis of Yingyin Guan Ying was a general under the grand commandant and requested Meng as a colonel.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Marquis Guan Ying served under the grand commandant and asked to have Guan Meng as a colonel.

context.previous: 父張孟，嘗為穎陰侯灌嬰舍人，得幸，因進之，至二千石，故蒙灌氏姓為灌孟。
context.next: 夫以千人與父俱。

translations.chinese: 夫以千人與父俱。
translations.literal: Fu accompanied his father with a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu followed his father with a thousand troops.

context.previous: 吳、楚反時，穎陰侯灌嬰為將軍，屬太尉，請孟為校尉。
context.next: 孟年老，穎陰侯強請之，鬱鬱不得意，故戰常陷堅，遂死吳軍中。

translations.chinese: 孟年老，穎陰侯強請之，鬱鬱不得意，故戰常陷堅，遂死吳軍中。
translations.literal: Meng was old; Marquis of Yingyin pressed him to serve despite his low spirits and discontent, so in battle he always charged the enemy's strongest points and died in the Wu army.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Meng was old; Marquis Guan Ying pressed him into the field despite his gloom, and he threw himself again and again at the enemy's hardest positions until he fell in the Wu lines.

context.previous: 夫以千人與父俱。
context.next: 漢法，父子俱，有死事，得與喪歸，夫不肯隨喪歸。

translations.chinese: 漢法，父子俱，有死事，得與喪歸，夫不肯隨喪歸。
translations.literal: Under Han law, when father and son both served and one died in service, the son might escort the coffin home; Fu refused to follow the funeral train home.
translations.idiomatic: Han statute allowed a son who served with his father to convoy the body home if the father died in battle; Guan Fu refused to leave with the funeral escort.

context.previous: 孟年老，穎陰侯強請之，鬱鬱不得意，故戰常陷堅，遂死吳軍中。
context.next: 奮曰：「願取吳王若將軍頭以報父仇！」

translations.chinese: 奮曰：「願取吳王若將軍頭以報父仇！」
translations.literal: He roused himself and said, "I would take the Prince of Wu's head, or the general's, to avenge my father's death!"
translations.idiomatic: He swore, "I will bring back the Prince of Wu's head—or the commander's—to avenge my father!"

context.previous: 漢法，父子俱，有死事，得與喪歸，夫不肯隨喪歸。
context.next: 於是夫被甲持戟，募軍中壯士所善願從數十人。

translations.chinese: 於是夫被甲持戟，募軍中壯士所善願從數十人。
translations.literal: Thereupon Fu donned armor, grasped a halberd, and enlisted several dozen stalwarts from the army who were his friends and willing to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He armored up, took a halberd, and rounded up several dozen volunteers from among his comrades in camp.

context.previous: 奮曰：「願取吳王若將軍頭以報父仇！」
context.next: 及出壁門，莫敢前。

translations.chinese: 及出壁門，莫敢前。
translations.literal: When they reached the camp gate, none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the palisade gate no one else dared go forward.

context.previous: 於是夫被甲持戟，募軍中壯士所善願從數十人。
context.next: 獨兩人及從奴十餘騎馳入吳軍，至戲下，所殺傷數十人。

translations.chinese: 獨兩人及從奴十餘騎馳入吳軍，至戲下，所殺傷數十人。
translations.literal: Only he and two others, with a dozen or so mounted slave attendants, galloped into the Wu army until they reached the general's banner, killing and wounding dozens.
translations.idiomatic: He and two companions, with a dozen mounted house slaves, charged deep into the Wu host as far as the command banner, cutting down dozens.

context.previous: 及出壁門，莫敢前。
context.next: 不得前，復還走漢壁，亡其奴，獨與一騎歸。

translations.chinese: 不得前，復還走漢壁，亡其奴，獨與一騎歸。
translations.literal: Unable to press forward, they turned back toward the Han camp; he lost his slaves and returned alone with one rider.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked from pushing farther, they wheeled back toward the Han lines; Guan Fu lost every follower but one horseman.

context.previous: 獨兩人及從奴十餘騎馳入吳軍，至戲下，所殺傷數十人。
context.next: 夫身中大創十餘，適有萬金良藥，故得無死。

translations.chinese: 夫身中大創十餘，適有萬金良藥，故得無死。
translations.literal: Fu himself suffered more than ten grievous wounds, but there happened to be a priceless salve worth ten thousand in cash, so he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: He took more than ten grave wounds but survived thanks to a ten-thousand-cash wound salve.

context.previous: 不得前，復還走漢壁，亡其奴，獨與一騎歸。
context.next: 創少瘳，又復請將軍曰：「吾益知吳壁曲折，請復往。」

translations.chinese: 創少瘳，又復請將軍曰：「吾益知吳壁曲折，請復往。」
translations.literal: When his wounds had healed a little, he again said to the general, "I understand the Wu camp's layout even better now; allow me to go again."
translations.idiomatic: When his cuts had closed a little, he told the general, "I know the Wu trenches even better now—let me go again."

context.previous: 夫身中大創十餘，適有萬金良藥，故得無死。
context.next: 將軍壯而義之，恐亡夫，乃言太尉，太尉召固止之。

translations.chinese: 將軍壯而義之，恐亡夫，乃言太尉，太尉召固止之。
translations.literal: The general admired him and thought him righteous, yet feared losing him; he reported to the grand commandant, who summoned him and firmly forbade another sortie.
translations.idiomatic: The general honored his courage but dared not lose him; he appealed to the grand commandant, who summoned Guan Fu and forbade another raid.

context.previous: 創少瘳，又復請將軍曰：「吾益知吳壁曲折，請復往。」
context.next: 吳軍破，夫以此名聞天下。

translations.chinese: 吳軍破，夫以此名聞天下。
translations.literal: When the Wu army was broken, Fu's name was known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was crushed, Guan Fu's name was known across the empire.

context.previous: 將軍壯而義之，恐亡夫，乃言太尉，太尉召固止之。

translations.chinese: 穎陰侯言夫，夫為郎中將。
translations.literal: Marquis of Yingyin spoke for Fu, and Fu was appointed general of the gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Guan Ying spoke for him, and Guan Fu was made general of the gentlemen.

context.next: 數歲，坐法去，家居長安中，諸公莫不稱，由是復為代相。

translations.chinese: 數歲，坐法去，家居長安中，諸公莫不稱，由是復為代相。
translations.literal: After several years he lost his office for breaking the law, lived at home in Chang'an, where no eminent man failed to praise him; on that account he was appointed chancellor of Dai again.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he lost his post for a legal offense and lived in Chang'an, where every notable sang his praises; he was therefore made chancellor of Dai once more.

context.previous: 穎陰侯言夫，夫為郎中將。

translations.chinese: 夫為人剛直，使酒，不好面諛。
translations.literal: Fu was by nature blunt and stubborn, abused wine when drinking, and disliked flattery to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu was blunt to a fault, a drunkard, and could not abide flatterers.

context.next: 貴戚諸勢在己之右，欲必陵之；

translations.chinese: 貴戚諸勢在己之右，欲必陵之；
translations.literal: As for noble in-laws and men of influence who stood to his right, he was determined to lord it over them;
translations.idiomatic: When some grandee or power broker outranked him, he made a point of humbling him;

context.previous: 夫為人剛直，使酒，不好面諛。
context.next: 士在己左，愈貧賤，尤益禮敬，與鈞。

translations.chinese: 士在己左，愈貧賤，尤益禮敬，與鈞。
translations.literal: for scholars to his left, the poorer and lower they were, the more he treated them with ritual respect, as equals.
translations.idiomatic: for humbler men on the social left, the poorer they were, the more courteously he treated them—as peers.

context.previous: 貴戚諸勢在己之右，欲必陵之；
context.next: 稠人廣眾，薦寵下輩。

translations.chinese: 稠人廣眾，薦寵下輩。
translations.literal: In thick crowds and broad assemblies he would recommend and honor those beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: In public he would praise and promote juniors.

context.previous: 士在己左，愈貧賤，尤益禮敬，與鈞。
context.next: 士亦以此多之。

translations.chinese: 士亦以此多之。
translations.literal: Scholars for this reason thought much of him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters admired him for it.

context.previous: 稠人廣眾，薦寵下輩。

translations.chinese: 夫不好文學，喜任俠，已然諾。
translations.literal: Fu did not care for literary learning; he delighted in acting the knight-errant and kept his word once given.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu had no taste for belles-lettres; he lived by the code of the bravo and kept every pledge.

context.next: 諸所與交通，無非豪桀大猾。

translations.chinese: 諸所與交通，無非豪桀大猾。
translations.literal: Of all with whom he associated, none were not bold spirits or great scoundrels.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone he ran with was either a swaggering tough or a hardened rogue.

context.previous: 夫不好文學，喜任俠，已然諾。
context.next: 家累數千萬，食客日數十百人。

translations.chinese: 家累數千萬，食客日數十百人。
translations.literal: His household wealth ran to several tens of millions in cash; his retainers numbered in the dozens or hundreds daily.
translations.idiomatic: His fortune ran into the tens of millions, and he fed dozens or hundreds of hangers-on every day.

context.previous: 諸所與交通，無非豪桀大猾。
context.next: 波池田園，宗族賓客為權利，橫穎川。

translations.chinese: 波池田園，宗族賓客為權利，橫穎川。
translations.literal: He had ponds, fields, and gardens; kinsmen and guests seized prerogatives and bullied their way across Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His ponds and estates sprawled wide; clan and clients muscled the magistrates and ran Yingchuan like a fief.

context.previous: 家累數千萬，食客日數十百人。
context.next: 穎川兒歌之曰：「穎水清，灌氏寧；

translations.chinese: 穎川兒歌之曰：「穎水清，灌氏寧；
translations.literal: The children of Yingchuan sang of it, saying, "When the Ying River runs clear, the Guan clan may rest;"
translations.idiomatic: Folk in Yingchuan sang, "Clear Ying water, the Guans may thrive;"

context.previous: 波池田園，宗族賓客為權利，橫穎川。
context.next: 穎水濁，灌氏族。」

translations.chinese: 穎水濁，灌氏族。」
translations.literal: "when the Ying River runs muddy, the Guan clan will perish."
translations.idiomatic: "muddy Ying water, wipe out the Guans."

context.previous: 穎川兒歌之曰：「穎水清，灌氏寧；

translations.chinese: 夫家居，卿相侍中賓客益衰。
translations.literal: When Fu lived at home, the guests of ministers and palace attendants grew ever fewer.
translations.idiomatic: At home his drawing room thinned out: fewer ministers and palace insiders called.

context.next: 及竇嬰失勢，亦欲倚夫引繩排根生平慕之後棄者。

translations.chinese: 及竇嬰失勢，亦欲倚夫引繩排根生平慕之後棄者。
translations.literal: When Dou Ying lost power, he too wished to lean on Fu to pull the line straight and root out those who in life had admired him but later cast him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Ying fell, he meant to use Guan Fu to settle old scores with fair-weather friends.

context.previous: 夫家居，卿相侍中賓客益衰。
context.next: 夫亦得嬰通列侯宗室為名高。

translations.chinese: 夫亦得嬰通列侯宗室為名高。
translations.literal: Fu in turn gained access through Ying to the marquises and imperial kin and thereby won a lofty name.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu, through Dou Ying, reached the marquises and the Liu clan—and borrowed their luster.

context.previous: 及竇嬰失勢，亦欲倚夫引繩排根生平慕之後棄者。
context.next: 兩人相為引重，其游如父子然，相得歡甚，無厭，恨相知之晚。

translations.chinese: 兩人相為引重，其游如父子然，相得歡甚，無厭，恨相知之晚。
translations.literal: The two men leaned on each other's weight; their association was like father and son, they suited each other with great delight and never tired, regretting only that they had not known each other sooner.
translations.idiomatic: They propped each other up like father and son, never tired of each other's company, and rued the day they had met so late.

context.previous: 夫亦得嬰通列侯宗室為名高。

translations.chinese: 夫嘗有服，過丞相蚡。
translations.literal: Fu once, while in mourning garb, passed Chancellor Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Once, still in mourning dress, Guan Fu called on Chancellor Tian Fen.

context.next: 蚡從容曰：「吾欲與仲孺過魏其侯，會仲孺有服。」

translations.chinese: 蚡從容曰：「吾欲與仲孺過魏其侯，會仲孺有服。」
translations.literal: Fen said at ease, "I would like to pass by Marquis of Weiqi with you, Zhongru, but you happen to be in mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen said lightly, "I had thought to visit Marquis Dou with you, Zhongru—but you are in mourning."

context.previous: 夫嘗有服，過丞相蚡。
context.next: 夫曰：「將軍乃肯幸臨況魏其侯，夫安敢以服為解！

translations.chinese: 夫曰：「將軍乃肯幸臨況魏其侯，夫安敢以服為解！
translations.literal: Fu said, "Would the general deign to honor Marquis of Weiqi with a visit—how dare I use mourning as an excuse!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu replied, "If a general of your rank will grace Dou Ying's door, how dare I hide behind mourning?"

context.previous: 蚡從容曰：「吾欲與仲孺過魏其侯，會仲孺有服。」
context.next: 請語魏其具，將軍旦日蚤臨。」

translations.chinese: 請語魏其具，將軍旦日蚤臨。」
translations.literal: "Please tell Marquis of Weiqi to prepare everything; the general will come early tomorrow morning."
translations.idiomatic: "Tell him to lay in everything; you will call early tomorrow."

context.previous: 夫曰：「將軍乃肯幸臨況魏其侯，夫安敢以服為解！
context.next: 蚡許諾。

translations.chinese: 蚡許諾。
translations.literal: Fen promised.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen agreed.

context.previous: 請語魏其具，將軍旦日蚤臨。」
context.next: 夫以語嬰。

translations.chinese: 夫以語嬰。
translations.literal: Fu told Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu carried the word to Dou Ying.

context.previous: 蚡許諾。
context.next: 嬰與夫人益市牛酒，夜灑掃張具至旦。

translations.chinese: 嬰與夫人益市牛酒，夜灑掃張具至旦。
translations.literal: Ying and his wife bought extra oxen and wine, swept and spread the furnishings by night until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying and his wife bought cattle and wine in quantity, cleaned the house, and set the hall from dusk till dawn.

context.previous: 夫以語嬰。
context.next: 平明，令門下侯司。

translations.chinese: 平明，令門下侯司。
translations.literal: At first light he ordered his gatemen to watch for the guest.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he posted servants to watch the road.

context.previous: 嬰與夫人益市牛酒，夜灑掃張具至旦。
context.next: 至日中，蚡不來。

translations.chinese: 至日中，蚡不來。
translations.literal: By midday Fen had not come.
translations.idiomatic: Noon passed; Tian Fen never appeared.

context.previous: 平明，令門下侯司。
context.next: 嬰謂夫曰：「丞相豈忘之哉？」

translations.chinese: 嬰謂夫曰：「丞相豈忘之哉？」
translations.literal: Ying said to Fu, "Has the chancellor forgotten?"
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying asked Guan Fu, "Has the chancellor forgotten us?"

context.previous: 至日中，蚡不來。
context.next: 夫不懌，曰：「夫以服請，不宜。」

translations.chinese: 夫不懌，曰：「夫以服請，不宜。」
translations.literal: Fu was displeased and said, "I asked him in mourning; he should not have agreed if it was improper."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu glowered. "I came to him in mourning; he had no business accepting if he never meant to come."

context.previous: 嬰謂夫曰：「丞相豈忘之哉？」
context.next: 乃駕，自往迎蚡。

translations.chinese: 乃駕，自往迎蚡。
translations.literal: Thereupon he harnessed his carriage and went himself to welcome Fen.
translations.idiomatic: He hitched his own chariot and drove to fetch Tian Fen.

context.previous: 夫不懌，曰：「夫以服請，不宜。」
context.next: 蚡特前戲許夫，殊無意往。

translations.chinese: 蚡特前戲許夫，殊無意往。
translations.literal: Fen had only jested and promised Fu earlier; he had absolutely no intention of going.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen had only been teasing when he said yes; he never meant to go.

context.previous: 乃駕，自往迎蚡。
context.next: 夫至門，蚡尚臥也。

translations.chinese: 夫至門，蚡尚臥也。
translations.literal: When Fu reached the gate, Fen was still abed.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Fu reached his gate, Tian Fen was still in bed.

context.previous: 蚡特前戲許夫，殊無意往。
context.next: 於是夫見，曰：「將軍昨日幸許過魏其，魏其夫妻治縣，至今未敢嘗食。」

translations.chinese: 於是夫見，曰：「將軍昨日幸許過魏其，魏其夫妻治縣，至今未敢嘗食。」
translations.literal: Thereupon Fu saw him and said, "Yesterday the general condescended to promise to visit Marquis of Weiqi; he and his wife have made every preparation since dawn and have not dared to eat."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu said to his face, "Yesterday you promised to visit Marquis Dou; he and his wife have laid in the feast since dawn and have not touched food."

context.previous: 夫至門，蚡尚臥也。
context.next: 蚡悟，謝曰：「吾醉，忘與仲孺言。」

translations.chinese: 蚡悟，謝曰：「吾醉，忘與仲孺言。」
translations.literal: Fen came to himself, apologized, and said, "I was drunk and forgot what I said to Zhongru."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen roused himself and apologized: "I was drunk and forgot my word to you."

context.previous: 於是夫見，曰：「將軍昨日幸許過魏其，魏其夫妻治縣，至今未敢嘗食。」
context.next: 乃駕往。

translations.chinese: 乃駕往。
translations.literal: Then he harnessed his carriage and went.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his carriage and set out.

context.previous: 蚡悟，謝曰：「吾醉，忘與仲孺言。」
context.next: 往又徐行，夫愈益怒。

translations.chinese: 往又徐行，夫愈益怒。
translations.literal: On the way he again went slowly; Fu grew only more furious.
translations.idiomatic: He crawled along the road; Guan Fu's rage mounted.

context.previous: 乃駕往。
context.next: 及飲酒酣，夫起舞屬蚡，蚡不起。

translations.chinese: 及飲酒酣，夫起舞屬蚡，蚡不起。
translations.literal: When they drank and the wine was deep, Fu rose to dance and handed the turn to Fen; Fen would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone round, Guan Fu rose to offer a dance and invited Tian Fen to follow; Tian Fen stayed seated.

context.previous: 往又徐行，夫愈益怒。
context.next: 夫徙坐，語侵之。

translations.chinese: 夫徙坐，語侵之。
translations.literal: Fu moved his mat and spoke words that insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu shifted his cushion and let fly a string of insults.

context.previous: 及飲酒酣，夫起舞屬蚡，蚡不起。
context.next: 嬰乃扶夫去，謝蚡。

translations.chinese: 嬰乃扶夫去，謝蚡。
translations.literal: Ying then supported Fu and led him away, apologizing to Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying helped Guan Fu out and apologized to Tian Fen.

context.previous: 夫徙坐，語侵之。
context.next: 蚡卒飲至夜，極歡而去。

translations.chinese: 蚡卒飲至夜，極歡而去。
translations.literal: Fen drank on until night and left in the utmost delight.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen drank till nightfall and left in high good humor.

context.previous: 嬰乃扶夫去，謝蚡。

translations.chinese: 後蚡使藉福請嬰城南田，嬰大望曰：「老僕雖棄，將軍雖貴，寧可以勢相奪乎！」
translations.literal: Later Fen sent Jifu to request of Ying the fields south of the city wall; Ying replied with great resentment, "Though this old servant has been cast aside, though the general is noble, how can he seize by force!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Tian Fen sent Jifu to ask for Dou Ying's fields south of the wall. Dou Ying flared: "I may be a discarded old fool and you a great minister, but you cannot bully me out of my land!"

context.next: 不許。

translations.chinese: 不許。
translations.literal: He did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

context.previous: 後蚡使藉福請嬰城南田，嬰大望曰：「老僕雖棄，將軍雖貴，寧可以勢相奪乎！」
context.next: 夫聞，怒罵福。

translations.chinese: 夫聞，怒罵福。
translations.literal: When Fu heard, he angrily cursed Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu heard and cursed Jifu roundly.

context.previous: 不許。
context.next: 福惡兩人有隙，乃謾好謝蚡曰：「魏其老且死，易忍，且待之。」

translations.chinese: 福惡兩人有隙，乃謾好謝蚡曰：「魏其老且死，易忍，且待之。」
translations.literal: Jifu hated that the two men had a rift; he therefore falsely spoke smooth words to apologize to Fen, saying, "Marquis of Weiqi is old and near death; he is easy to endure; wait a while for him."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu feared a breach between them, so he lied smoothly to Tian Fen: "Dou Ying is old and dying; you can afford to wait him out."

context.previous: 夫聞，怒罵福。
context.next: 已而蚡聞嬰、夫實怒不予，亦怒曰：「魏其子嘗殺人，蚡活之。

translations.chinese: 已而蚡聞嬰、夫實怒不予，亦怒曰：「魏其子嘗殺人，蚡活之。
translations.literal: Before long Fen heard that Ying and Fu were truly angry and would not give; he too grew angry and said, "Marquis of Weiqi's son once killed a man; I saved his life."
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Fen learned they truly refused, he snarled, "Dou Ying's son once committed murder; I spared him."

context.previous: 福惡兩人有隙，乃謾好謝蚡曰：「魏其老且死，易忍，且待之。」
context.next: 蚡事魏其無所不可，愛數頃田？

translations.chinese: 蚡事魏其無所不可，愛數頃田？
translations.literal: "In serving Marquis of Weiqi I have denied him nothing—does he begrudge me a few qing of fields?"
translations.idiomatic: "I have refused Dou Ying nothing—does he grudge me a few hectares?"

context.previous: 已而蚡聞嬰、夫實怒不予，亦怒曰：「魏其子嘗殺人，蚡活之。
context.next: 且灌夫何與也？

translations.chinese: 且灌夫何與也？
translations.literal: "Moreover what has Guan Fu to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: "And what business is it of Guan Fu's?"

context.previous: 蚡事魏其無所不可，愛數頃田？
context.next: 吾不敢復求田！」

translations.chinese: 吾不敢復求田！」
translations.literal: "I dare not ask for fields again!"
translations.idiomatic: "I will never ask for that land again!"

context.previous: 且灌夫何與也？
context.next: 由此大怒。

translations.chinese: 由此大怒。
translations.literal: From this he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: From that day his hatred ran deep.

context.previous: 吾不敢復求田！」

translations.chinese: 元光四年春，蚡言灌夫家在穎川，橫甚，民苦之。
translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Yuanguang, Fen said that Guan Fu's family was in Yingchuan and was extremely overbearing; the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yuanguang 4, Tian Fen reported that the Guan clan tyrannized Yingchuan and the commoners groaned under them.

context.next: 請案之。

translations.chinese: 請案之。
translations.literal: He requested that it be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to open an inquiry.

context.previous: 元光四年春，蚡言灌夫家在穎川，橫甚，民苦之。
context.next: 上曰：「此丞相事，何請？」

translations.chinese: 上曰：「此丞相事，何請？」
translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is the chancellor's affair; why ask?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is the chancellor's business—why petition me?"

context.previous: 請案之。
context.next: 夫亦持蚡陰事，為奸利，受淮南王金與語言。

translations.chinese: 夫亦持蚡陰事，為奸利，受淮南王金與語言。
translations.literal: Fu in turn held Fen's secret affairs—illicit profit, accepting gold from the Prince of Huainan, and promises in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu held Tian Fen's secrets—bribes, gold from the king of Huainan, and treasonous talk.

context.previous: 上曰：「此丞相事，何請？」
context.next: 賓客居間，遂已，俱解。

translations.chinese: 賓客居間，遂已，俱解。
translations.literal: Guests mediated between them, and in the end it stopped; both sides backed off.
translations.idiomatic: Friends brokered a truce, and both sides let the matter drop—for the moment.

context.previous: 夫亦持蚡陰事，為奸利，受淮南王金與語言。

translations.chinese: 夏，蚡取燕王女為夫人，太后詔召列侯宗室皆往賀。
translations.literal: In summer Fen took the daughter of the Prince of Yan as his wife; the empress dowager issued an edict summoning all marquises and imperial kin to attend the celebration.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Tian Fen married a daughter of the Prince of Yan; the empress dowager ordered every noble and Liu kinsman to the wedding feast.

context.next: 嬰過夫，欲與俱。

translations.chinese: 嬰過夫，欲與俱。
translations.literal: Ying passed by Fu and wished to go together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying stopped at Guan Fu's and asked him along.

context.previous: 夏，蚡取燕王女為夫人，太后詔召列侯宗室皆往賀。
context.next: 夫謝曰：「夫數以酒失過丞相，丞相今者又與夫有隙。」

translations.chinese: 夫謝曰：「夫數以酒失過丞相，丞相今者又與夫有隙。」
translations.literal: Fu declined, saying, "I have often given offense to the chancellor through wine; the chancellor and I now have a rift as well."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu begged off: "I have insulted the chancellor too often when drunk, and we are already at odds."

context.previous: 嬰過夫，欲與俱。
context.next: 嬰曰：「事已解。」

translations.chinese: 嬰曰：「事已解。」
translations.literal: Ying said, "The affair is already settled."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying said, "That is all patched up."

context.previous: 夫謝曰：「夫數以酒失過丞相，丞相今者又與夫有隙。」
context.next: 強與俱。

translations.chinese: 強與俱。
translations.literal: He forced him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged him along anyway.

context.previous: 嬰曰：「事已解。」
context.next: 酒酣，蚡起為壽，坐皆避席伏。

translations.chinese: 酒酣，蚡起為壽，坐皆避席伏。
translations.literal: When the wine was deep, Fen rose to offer a toast of longevity; all those seated left their mats and knelt prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone round, Tian Fen rose to propose a toast; every guest left his cushion and knelt in respect.

context.previous: 強與俱。
context.next: 已嬰為壽，獨故人避席，余半膝席。

translations.chinese: 已嬰為壽，獨故人避席，余半膝席。
translations.literal: When Ying offered his toast of longevity, only old friends left their mats; the rest knelt on one knee on their mats.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Ying did the same, only old friends rose fully; the others merely hitched forward on one knee.

context.previous: 酒酣，蚡起為壽，坐皆避席伏。
context.next: 夫行酒，至蚡，蚡膝席曰：「不能滿觴。」

translations.chinese: 夫行酒，至蚡，蚡膝席曰：「不能滿觴。」
translations.literal: When Fu passed the wine to Fen, Fen knelt on his mat and said, "I cannot empty the cup."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu poured for Tian Fen, who stayed on his cushion and said, "I cannot drain the cup."

context.previous: 已嬰為壽，獨故人避席，余半膝席。
context.next: 夫怒，因嘻笑曰：「將軍貴人也，畢之！」

translations.chinese: 夫怒，因嘻笑曰：「將軍貴人也，畢之！」
translations.literal: Fu was angry and, with a mocking laugh, said, "The general is a noble man—finish it!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu sneered, "You are a great man, General—drink it down!"

context.previous: 夫行酒，至蚡，蚡膝席曰：「不能滿觴。」
context.next: 時蚡不肯。

translations.chinese: 時蚡不肯。
translations.literal: At the time Fen would not.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen still refused.

context.previous: 夫怒，因嘻笑曰：「將軍貴人也，畢之！」
context.next: 行酒次至臨汝侯灌賢，賢方與程不識耳語，又不避席。

translations.chinese: 行酒次至臨汝侯灌賢，賢方與程不識耳語，又不避席。
translations.literal: When passing the wine he next came to Marquis of Linying Guan Xian; Xian was whispering in Cheng Bushi's ear and did not leave his mat.
translations.idiomatic: Next he reached Marquis Guan Xian of Linying, who was whispering to Cheng Bushi and never rose from his mat.

context.previous: 時蚡不肯。
context.next: 夫無所發怒，乃罵賢曰：「平生毀程不識不直一錢，今日長者為壽，乃效女曹兒呫囁耳語！」

translations.chinese: 夫無所發怒，乃罵賢曰：「平生毀程不識不直一錢，今日長者為壽，乃效女曹兒呫囁耳語！」
translations.literal: Fu had nowhere else to vent his anger; he therefore cursed Xian, saying, "All your life you have slandered Cheng Bushi as not worth a cash; today when an elder offers a toast of longevity, you imitate girls and children whispering in the ear!"
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere else to vent, Guan Fu turned on Guan Xian: "You have always called Cheng Bushi worthless—now an elder proposes a toast and you sit there simpering like women in a corner!"

context.previous: 行酒次至臨汝侯灌賢，賢方與程不識耳語，又不避席。
context.next: 蚡謂夫曰：「程、李俱東西宮衛尉，今眾辱程將軍，仲孺獨不為李將軍地乎？」

translations.chinese: 蚡謂夫曰：「程、李俱東西宮衛尉，今眾辱程將軍，仲孺獨不為李將軍地乎？」
translations.literal: Fen said to Fu, "Cheng and Li are both commandants of the eastern and western palaces; today you have publicly humiliated General Cheng—will Zhongru show no consideration for General Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen said, "Cheng Bushi and Li Guang are commandants of the eastern and western palaces; you have shamed Cheng in public—do you spare no face for Li Guang?"

context.previous: 夫無所發怒，乃罵賢曰：「平生毀程不識不直一錢，今日長者為壽，乃效女曹兒呫囁耳語！」
context.next: 夫曰：「今曰斬頭穴匈，何知程、李！」

translations.chinese: 夫曰：「今曰斬頭穴匈，何知程、李！」
translations.literal: Fu said, "I would rather be beheaded and disemboweled—what are Cheng and Li to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu roared, "I would rather lose my head and rip open my chest—what are Cheng Bushi and Li Guang to me?"

context.previous: 蚡謂夫曰：「程、李俱東西宮衛尉，今眾辱程將軍，仲孺獨不為李將軍地乎？」
context.next: 坐乃起更衣，稍稍去。

translations.chinese: 坐乃起更衣，稍稍去。
translations.literal: Those seated then rose to change clothes and gradually departed.
translations.idiomatic: The guests rose to "change clothes" and slipped away one by one.

context.previous: 夫曰：「今曰斬頭穴匈，何知程、李！」
context.next: 嬰去，戲夫。

translations.chinese: 嬰去，戲夫。
translations.literal: When Ying left, he jested with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying left with a joking word to Guan Fu.

context.previous: 坐乃起更衣，稍稍去。
context.next: 夫出，蚡遂怒曰：「此吾驕灌夫罪也。」

translations.chinese: 夫出，蚡遂怒曰：「此吾驕灌夫罪也。」
translations.literal: When Fu went out, Fen then angrily said, "This is my fault for indulging Guan Fu."
translations.idiomatic: As Guan Fu left, Tian Fen snarled, "I have only myself to blame for spoiling him."

context.previous: 嬰去，戲夫。
context.next: 乃令騎留夫，夫不得出。

translations.chinese: 乃令騎留夫，夫不得出。
translations.literal: He ordered mounted guards to detain Fu; Fu could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered horsemen to bar the door; Guan Fu could not get out.

context.previous: 夫出，蚡遂怒曰：「此吾驕灌夫罪也。」
context.next: 藉福起為謝，案夫項令謝。

translations.chinese: 藉福起為謝，案夫項令謝。
translations.literal: Jifu rose to apologize, pressed Fu by the neck, and ordered him to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu stood to mediate, seized Guan Fu by the neck, and tried to force a bow of apology.

context.previous: 乃令騎留夫，夫不得出。
context.next: 夫愈怒，不肯順。

translations.chinese: 夫愈怒，不肯順。
translations.literal: Fu grew only more angry and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu only grew more furious and would not yield.

context.previous: 藉福起為謝，案夫項令謝。
context.next: 蚡乃戲騎縛夫置傳捨，召長史曰：「今日召宗室，有詔。」

translations.chinese: 蚡乃戲騎縛夫置傳捨，召長史曰：「今日召宗室，有詔。」
translations.literal: Fen then jokingly ordered the mounted guards to bind Fu and place him in the relay lodge; he summoned the chief clerk and said, "Today I summoned the imperial kin; there was an edict."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen had his riders tie Guan Fu and dump him in the post station, then called his chief clerk: "Today's gathering was by imperial summons."

context.previous: 夫愈怒，不肯順。
context.next: 劾灌夫罵坐不敬，系居室。

translations.chinese: 劾灌夫罵坐不敬，系居室。
translations.literal: He impeached Guan Fu for cursing those seated and showing disrespect; he bound him in the detention quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Guan Fu with insulting the guests and lack of respect, and threw him in the palace jail.

context.previous: 蚡乃戲騎縛夫置傳捨，召長史曰：「今日召宗室，有詔。」
context.next: 遂其前事，遣吏分曹逐捕諸灌氏支屬，皆得棄市罪。

translations.chinese: 遂其前事，遣吏分曹逐捕諸灌氏支屬，皆得棄市罪。
translations.literal: He pursued his earlier accusations, sent clerks in separate teams to hunt down every branch of the Guan clan, and all were found guilty of execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He revived old charges, sent officers to round up every Guan kinsman, and fixed them all with the death penalty.

context.previous: 劾灌夫罵坐不敬，系居室。
context.next: 嬰愧，為資使賓客請，莫能解。

translations.chinese: 嬰愧，為資使賓客請，莫能解。
translations.literal: Ying was ashamed; he supplied funds and had guests plead, but none could undo it.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying was mortified; he spent his fortune on intermediaries, but no one could free him.

context.previous: 遂其前事，遣吏分曹逐捕諸灌氏支屬，皆得棄市罪。
context.next: 蚡吏皆為耳目，諸灌氏皆仁匿，夫系，遂不得告言蚡陰事。

translations.chinese: 蚡吏皆為耳目，諸灌氏皆仁匿，夫系，遂不得告言蚡陰事。
translations.literal: Fen's clerks were all his eyes and ears; every branch of the Guan clan had fled into hiding; with Fu bound, he could not report Fen's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen's men watched every move; the Guan kinsmen had all gone to ground; with Guan Fu in chains, no one could denounce Tian Fen's secrets.

context.previous: 嬰愧，為資使賓客請，莫能解。

translations.chinese: 嬰銳為救夫，嬰夫人諫曰：「灌將軍得罪丞相，與太后家迕，寧可救邪？」
translations.literal: Ying was keen to save Fu; Ying's wife remonstrated, saying, "General Guan has offended the chancellor and crossed the empress dowager's house—can he possibly be saved?"
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying was bent on saving Guan Fu. His wife warned him, "Guan Fu has insulted the chancellor and defied the Tian family—can you save him?"

context.next: 嬰曰：「侯自我得之，自我捐之，無所恨。

translations.chinese: 嬰曰：「侯自我得之，自我捐之，無所恨。
translations.literal: Ying said, "The marquisate I won for myself I may cast away for myself; I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying said, "I won my title with my own merit; I may lose it the same way—I have no regrets."

context.previous: 嬰銳為救夫，嬰夫人諫曰：「灌將軍得罪丞相，與太后家迕，寧可救邪？」
context.next: 且終不令灌仲孺獨死，嬰獨生。」

translations.chinese: 且終不令灌仲孺獨死，嬰獨生。」
translations.literal: "Moreover in the end I will not allow Guan Zhongru to die alone while I, Ying, live."
translations.idiomatic: "Nor will I let Guan Zhongru die while I alone survive."

context.previous: 嬰曰：「侯自我得之，自我捐之，無所恨。
context.next: 乃匿其家，竊出上書。

translations.chinese: 乃匿其家，竊出上書。
translations.literal: Thereupon he hid it from his family, stole out, and submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped past his household, stole out, and filed a memorial with the throne.

context.previous: 且終不令灌仲孺獨死，嬰獨生。」
context.next: 立召人，具告言灌夫醉飽事，不足誅。

translations.chinese: 立召人，具告言灌夫醉飽事，不足誅。
translations.literal: He immediately summoned a man in and fully reported Guan Fu's drunken surfeit affair, saying it did not merit execution.
translations.idiomatic: He had Guan Fu brought in at once and laid out the whole drunken-scene story, arguing it did not merit death.

context.previous: 乃匿其家，竊出上書。
context.next: 上然之，賜嬰食，曰：「東朝廷辯之。」

translations.chinese: 上然之，賜嬰食，曰：「東朝廷辯之。」
translations.literal: The emperor agreed, gave Ying a meal, and said, "Debate it in the eastern court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented, fed Dou Ying, and said, "Argue it out in the eastern court."

context.previous: 立召人，具告言灌夫醉飽事，不足誅。

translations.chinese: 嬰東朝，盛推夫善，言其醉飽得過，乃丞相以它事誣罪之。
translations.literal: Ying went to the eastern court and greatly praised Fu's goodness, saying his offense was drunken surfeit, and that the chancellor had falsely accused him on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern court Dou Ying praised Guan Fu to the skies, blamed the brawl on drink, and called Tian Fen's charges a frame-up.

context.next: 蚡盛毀夫所為橫恣，罪逆不道。

translations.chinese: 蚡盛毀夫所為橫恣，罪逆不道。
translations.literal: Fen greatly slandered Fu's conduct as violent and arbitrary, criminal and contrary to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen blackened Guan Fu as a bully whose crimes knew no law.

context.previous: 嬰東朝，盛推夫善，言其醉飽得過，乃丞相以它事誣罪之。
context.next: 嬰度無可奈何，因言蚡短。

translations.chinese: 嬰度無可奈何，因言蚡短。
translations.literal: Ying, estimating there was nothing to be done, therefore spoke of Fen's shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he was losing, Dou Ying turned to Tian Fen's own faults.

context.previous: 蚡盛毀夫所為橫恣，罪逆不道。
context.next: 蚡曰：「天下幸而安樂無事，蚡得為肺附，所好音樂、狗馬、田宅，所愛倡優、巧匠之屬，不如魏其、灌夫日夜招聚天下豪傑壯士與論議，腹誹而心謗，卬視天，俯畫地，辟睨兩官間，幸天下有變，而欲有大功。

translations.chinese: 蚡曰：「天下幸而安樂無事，蚡得為肺附，所好音樂、狗馬、田宅，所愛倡優、巧匠之屬，不如魏其、灌夫日夜招聚天下豪傑壯士與論議，腹誹而心謗，卬視天，俯畫地，辟睨兩官間，幸天下有變，而欲有大功。
translations.literal: Fen said, "So long as the realm is fortunate enough to be at peace and without incident, I, Fen, have been able to be kin to the throne; what I love are music, dogs, horses, fields, and houses; what I cherish are singers, actors, and clever craftsmen—I am not like Marquis of Weiqi and Guan Fu, who day and night gather the bold spirits and stalwarts of the realm to debate with them, who slander in the belly and revile in the heart, who look up to mark the sky and look down to trace the earth, who squint between the two palaces, hoping the realm will meet with change so they may win great merit."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen said, "While the empire enjoys peace, I, as the emperor's uncle, care for music, hounds, horses, and mansions—singers, actors, and craftsmen. I am nothing like Dou Ying and Guan Fu, who recruit ruffians day and night, nurse private grudges, scan heaven and earth, and leer toward both palaces, praying for turmoil so they can seize glory."

context.previous: 嬰度無可奈何，因言蚡短。
context.next: 臣乃不如魏其等所為。」

translations.chinese: 臣乃不如魏其等所為。」
translations.literal: "I am indeed not equal to what Marquis of Weiqi and the others do."
translations.idiomatic: "I am not in their league."

context.previous: 蚡曰：「天下幸而安樂無事，蚡得為肺附，所好音樂、狗馬、田宅，所愛倡優、巧匠之屬，不如魏其、灌夫日夜招聚天下豪傑壯士與論議，腹誹而心謗，卬視天，俯畫地，辟睨兩官間，幸天下有變，而欲有大功。
context.next: 上問朝臣：「兩人孰是？」

translations.chinese: 上問朝臣：「兩人孰是？」
translations.literal: The emperor asked the court ministers, "Which of the two is right?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, "Who speaks truth?"

context.previous: 臣乃不如魏其等所為。」
context.next: 御史大夫韓安國曰：「魏其言灌夫父死事，身荷戟馳不測之吳軍，身被數十創，名冠三軍，此天下壯士，非有大惡，爭杯酒，不足引它過以誅也。

translations.chinese: 御史大夫韓安國曰：「魏其言灌夫父死事，身荷戟馳不測之吳軍，身被數十創，名冠三軍，此天下壯士，非有大惡，爭杯酒，不足引它過以誅也。
translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Han Anguo said, "As Marquis of Weiqi says, Guan Fu's father died in service; he himself shouldered a halberd and galloped into the immeasurable Wu army, his body suffering dozens of wounds; his fame crowned the three armies—he is a stalwart of the realm. Unless he has committed some great evil, to wring another fault from a quarrel over cups of wine is not enough ground for execution."
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said, "Dou Ying is right that Guan Fu's father died in battle while the son, halberd in hand, charged the Wu lines and took dozens of wounds—a hero of the empire. Without a graver crime than a wine quarrel, he should not die for it."

context.previous: 上問朝臣：「兩人孰是？」
context.next: 魏其言是。

translations.chinese: 魏其言是。
translations.literal: What Marquis of Weiqi says is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Dou speaks the truth.

context.previous: 御史大夫韓安國曰：「魏其言灌夫父死事，身荷戟馳不測之吳軍，身被數十創，名冠三軍，此天下壯士，非有大惡，爭杯酒，不足引它過以誅也。
context.next: 丞相亦言灌夫通姦猾，侵細民，家累巨萬，橫恣穎川，□轢宗室，侵犯骨肉，此所謂『支大於干，脛大於股，不折必披』。

translations.chinese: 丞相亦言灌夫通姦猾，侵細民，家累巨萬，橫恣穎川，□轢宗室，侵犯骨肉，此所謂『支大於干，脛大於股，不折必披』。
translations.literal: The chancellor also says that Guan Fu associates with crafty scoundrels, bullies the common people, his household wealth piles to vast sums, he runs riot in Yingchuan, tramples the imperial house, and violates flesh-and-blood kin—this is what is called "when the branch is greater than the trunk, when the shin is greater than the thigh, if it does not break it will split."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor is also right: Guan Fu consorts with villains, preys on the weak, has piled up a fortune, tyrannizes Yingchuan, rides roughshod over the imperial clan, and wrongs his own blood—what the proverb calls a limb thicker than the trunk, a calf thicker than the thigh: something must snap.

context.previous: 魏其言是。
context.next: 丞相信亦是。

translations.chinese: 丞相信亦是。
translations.literal: What the chancellor says is also correct.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor speaks truth as well.

context.previous: 丞相亦言灌夫通姦猾，侵細民，家累巨萬，橫恣穎川，□轢宗室，侵犯骨肉，此所謂『支大於干，脛大於股，不折必披』。
context.next: 唯明主裁之。」

translations.chinese: 唯明主裁之。」
translations.literal: "Let the enlightened ruler decide."
translations.idiomatic: "Only Your Majesty can judge."

context.previous: 丞相信亦是。
context.next: 主爵都尉汲黯是魏其。

translations.chinese: 主爵都尉汲黯是魏其。
translations.literal: Chief Commandant of the Nobility Ji An sided with Marquis of Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An, chief commandant of the nobility, backed Dou Ying.

context.previous: 唯明主裁之。」
context.next: 內史鄭當時是魏其，後不堅。

translations.chinese: 內史鄭當時是魏其，後不堅。
translations.literal: Palace Secretary Zheng Dangshi sided with Marquis of Weiqi, but later did not hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Palace secretary Zheng Dangshi began on Dou Ying's side, then wavered.

context.previous: 主爵都尉汲黯是魏其。
context.next: 餘皆莫敢對。

translations.chinese: 餘皆莫敢對。
translations.literal: The rest all dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The others held their tongues.

context.previous: 內史鄭當時是魏其，後不堅。
context.next: 上怒內史曰：「公平生數言魏其、武安長短，今日廷論，局趣效轅下駒，吾並斬若屬矣！」

translations.chinese: 上怒內史曰：「公平生數言魏其、武安長短，今日廷論，局趣效轅下駒，吾並斬若屬矣！」
translations.literal: The emperor grew angry at the palace secretary and said, "You, sir, have all your life often spoken of the strengths and weaknesses of Marquis of Weiqi and Marquis of Wu'an; today at court debate you are cramped and act like a colt under the shafts—I will behead the lot of you!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned on Zheng Dangshi: "You have spent years weighing Dou Ying against Tian Fen; today at court you freeze like a colt between the traces—I could behead you all!"

context.previous: 餘皆莫敢對。
context.next: 即罷起入，上食太后。

translations.chinese: 即罷起入，上食太后。
translations.literal: Immediately he stopped, rose, and entered; he took his meal with the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the session short, rose, and withdrew to dine with his mother.

context.previous: 上怒內史曰：「公平生數言魏其、武安長短，今日廷論，局趣效轅下駒，吾並斬若屬矣！」
context.next: 太后亦已使人候司，具以語太后。

translations.chinese: 太后亦已使人候司，具以語太后。
translations.literal: The empress dowager had already sent someone to watch and report; they fully told the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: She had already posted spies; they told her everything.

context.previous: 即罷起入，上食太后。
context.next: 太后怒，不食，曰：「我在也，而人皆藉吾弟，令我百歲後，皆魚肉之乎！

translations.chinese: 太后怒，不食，曰：「我在也，而人皆藉吾弟，令我百歲後，皆魚肉之乎！
translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry, would not eat, and said, "While I am still alive, they all trample my younger brother; after I reach a hundred years, will they carve him up like fish meat!"
translations.idiomatic: She refused her meal in fury: "I am still alive, yet they walk on my brother; when I am gone, will they cut him to pieces?"

context.previous: 太后亦已使人候司，具以語太后。
context.next: 且帝寧能為石人邪！

translations.chinese: 且帝寧能為石人邪！
translations.literal: "Moreover can the emperor really be a stone man!"
translations.idiomatic: "And is the emperor a block of stone, deaf to his own mother?"

context.previous: 太后怒，不食，曰：「我在也，而人皆藉吾弟，令我百歲後，皆魚肉之乎！
context.next: 此特帝在，即錄錄，設百歲後，是屬寧有可信者乎？」

translations.chinese: 此特帝在，即錄錄，設百歲後，是屬寧有可信者乎？」
translations.literal: This is only while the emperor is alive that they are submissive and timid; suppose after a hundred years—can any of this lot be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: Only while you sit on the throne do they cringe; once you are gone, would you trust a single one of them?"

context.previous: 且帝寧能為石人邪！
context.next: 上謝曰：「俱外家，故廷辨之。

translations.chinese: 上謝曰：「俱外家，故廷辨之。
translations.literal: The emperor apologized and said, "They are both maternal kin, therefore I debated them at court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor apologized: "Both sides are my in-laws—that is why I aired the dispute in open court."

context.previous: 此特帝在，即錄錄，設百歲後，是屬寧有可信者乎？」
context.next: 不然，此一獄吏所決耳。」

translations.chinese: 不然，此一獄吏所決耳。」
translations.literal: "If not for that, this would be something a single jail clerk could decide."
translations.idiomatic: "Otherwise a county jailer could have settled it."

context.previous: 上謝曰：「俱外家，故廷辨之。
context.next: 是時，郎中令石建為上分別言兩人。

translations.chinese: 是時，郎中令石建為上分別言兩人。
translations.literal: At that time the supervisor of the household Shi Jian separately explained the two men to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the household Shi Jian then gave the emperor a private briefing on each man.

context.previous: 不然，此一獄吏所決耳。」

translations.chinese: 蚡已罷朝，出止車門，召御史大夫安國載，怒曰：「與長孺共一禿翁，何為首鼠兩端？」
translations.literal: When Fen had finished court and went out, he stopped at the carriage gate, summoned Censor-in-chief Anguo to ride in his carriage, and angrily said, "You and Changru were scheming over one bald old man—why waver between two sides?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen left court, halted at the gate, pulled Han Anguo into his chariot, and fumed, "You and I were advising against the same graybeard—why play both sides now?"

context.next: 安國良久謂蚡曰：「君何不自喜！

translations.chinese: 安國良久謂蚡曰：「君何不自喜！
translations.literal: Anguo was silent a long time, then said to Fen, "Why are you not pleased with yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence Han Anguo said, "You might show a little self-satisfaction."

context.previous: 蚡已罷朝，出止車門，召御史大夫安國載，怒曰：「與長孺共一禿翁，何為首鼠兩端？」
context.next: 夫魏其毀君，君當免冠解印綬歸，曰『臣以肺附幸得待罪，固非其任，魏其言皆是。』

translations.chinese: 夫魏其毀君，君當免冠解印綬歸，曰『臣以肺附幸得待罪，固非其任，魏其言皆是。』
translations.literal: "When Marquis of Weiqi slanders you, you ought to remove your cap, untie your seal cord, and retire, saying, 'I have been privileged to hold office as the emperor's kin; it is truly not my competence; what Marquis of Weiqi says is all correct.'"
translations.idiomatic: "When Dou Ying attacks you, take off your cap, hand back your seal, and say: I am only the emperor's uncle-by-marriage; the post is beyond me; Dou Ying speaks the truth."

context.previous: 安國良久謂蚡曰：「君何不自喜！
context.next: 如此，上必多君有讓，不廢君。

translations.chinese: 如此，上必多君有讓，不廢君。
translations.literal: "Thus the emperor is sure to think much of you for yielding and will not dismiss you."
translations.idiomatic: "The throne will honor you for stepping aside and will not cast you off."

context.previous: 夫魏其毀君，君當免冠解印綬歸，曰『臣以肺附幸得待罪，固非其任，魏其言皆是。』
context.next: 魏其必愧，杜門齒齰舌自殺。

translations.chinese: 魏其必愧，杜門齒齰舌自殺。
translations.literal: Marquis of Weiqi would be ashamed, bolt his gates, gnash his teeth and tongue, and kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying would die of shame behind bolted doors—perhaps even by his own hand.

context.previous: 如此，上必多君有讓，不廢君。
context.next: 今人毀君，君亦毀之，譬如要豎女子爭言，何其無大體也！」

translations.chinese: 今人毀君，君亦毀之，譬如要豎女子爭言，何其無大體也！」
translations.literal: "Now others slander you and you slander them in turn—it is like washerwomen and girls quarreling in words; how lacking in great deportment!"
translations.idiomatic: "Instead you trade insults like market women—where is the dignity of a minister?"

context.previous: 魏其必愧，杜門齒齰舌自殺。
context.next: 蚡謝曰：「爭時爭，不知出此。」

translations.chinese: 蚡謝曰：「爭時爭，不知出此。」
translations.literal: Fen apologized and said, "In the heat of dispute I disputed; I did not know to produce this."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Fen apologized: "I was carried away in the fight; I never thought of your stratagem."

context.previous: 今人毀君，君亦毀之，譬如要豎女子爭言，何其無大體也！」

translations.chinese: 於是上使御史簿責嬰所言灌夫頗不讎，劾繫都司空。
translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered the censor to register and call Ying to account for what he had said about Guan Fu, which largely did not match; he impeached him and bound him in the metropolitan superintendent's custody.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the censor cross-examine Dou Ying: his claims about Guan Fu did not check out; he was impeached and jailed under the metropolitan superintendent.

context.next: 孝景時，嬰嘗受遺詔，曰「事有不便，以便宜論上」。

translations.chinese: 孝景時，嬰嘗受遺詔，曰「事有不便，以便宜論上」。
translations.literal: Under Emperor Jing, Ying had once received a testamentary edict saying, "If affairs are inconvenient, you may memorialize at your discretion on what is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing had once given Dou Ying a sealed rescript: "If state business goes awry, memorialize as you see fit."

context.previous: 於是上使御史簿責嬰所言灌夫頗不讎，劾繫都司空。
context.next: 及系，灌夫罪至族，事日急，諸公莫敢復明言於上。

translations.chinese: 及系，灌夫罪至族，事日急，諸公莫敢復明言於上。
translations.literal: By the time he was bound, Guan Fu's crime reached to clan extermination; the affair grew urgent daily, and no grandee dared speak plainly again to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: By then Guan Fu faced extermination of his clan; the case raced toward verdict, and no minister dared speak for Dou Ying at court.

context.previous: 孝景時，嬰嘗受遺詔，曰「事有不便，以便宜論上」。
context.next: 嬰乃使昆弟子上書言之，幸得召見。

translations.chinese: 嬰乃使昆弟子上書言之，幸得召見。
translations.literal: Ying then had a nephew submit a memorial on it, hoping to obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying smuggled a memorial out through a nephew, hoping for a summons.

context.previous: 及系，灌夫罪至族，事日急，諸公莫敢復明言於上。
context.next: 書奏，案尚書，大行無遺詔。

translations.chinese: 書奏，案尚書，大行無遺詔。
translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, they checked the Minister of Documents' archives; the Minister of Funerals reported there was no testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the document arrived, the archives of the Minister of Documents were searched; the office of the grand coach reported no such testament on file.

context.previous: 嬰乃使昆弟子上書言之，幸得召見。
context.next: 詔書獨臧嬰家，嬰家丞封。

translations.chinese: 詔書獨臧嬰家，嬰家丞封。
translations.literal: The edict text alone was stored in Ying's house; Ying's household steward had sealed it.
translations.idiomatic: The only copy of the alleged edict had lain in Dou Ying's house under his steward's seal.

context.previous: 書奏，案尚書，大行無遺詔。
context.next: 乃劾嬰矯先帝詔害，罪當棄市。

translations.chinese: 乃劾嬰矯先帝詔害，罪當棄市。
translations.literal: Thereupon they impeached Ying for forging the late emperor's edict to do harm; the crime merited execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with forging a dead emperor's edict—a capital offense.

context.previous: 詔書獨臧嬰家，嬰家丞封。
context.next: 五年十月，悉論灌夫支屬。

translations.chinese: 五年十月，悉論灌夫支屬。
translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year, they sentenced all branches of Guan Fu's kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year the entire Guan clan was condemned.

context.previous: 乃劾嬰矯先帝詔害，罪當棄市。
context.next: 嬰良久乃聞有劾，即陽病痱，不食慾死。

translations.chinese: 嬰良久乃聞有劾，即陽病痱，不食慾死。
translations.literal: Only after a long time did Ying hear of the impeachment; then he feigned apoplexy, would not eat, and wished to die.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying learned of the impeachment late; he feigned a stroke, refused food, and prepared to die.

context.previous: 五年十月，悉論灌夫支屬。
context.next: 或聞上無意殺嬰，復食，治病，議定不死矣。

translations.chinese: 或聞上無意殺嬰，復食，治病，議定不死矣。
translations.literal: Some heard that the emperor had no intention of killing Ying; he ate again, treated his illness, and they reckoned he would surely not die.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that the emperor would spare him; he took food again, nursed his health, and his friends thought he was safe.

context.previous: 嬰良久乃聞有劾，即陽病痱，不食慾死。
context.next: 乃有飛語為惡言聞上，故以十二月晦論棄市渭城。

translations.chinese: 乃有飛語為惡言聞上，故以十二月晦論棄市渭城。
translations.literal: Then flying rumors of evil words reached the emperor; therefore on the last day of the twelfth month he was sentenced to execution in the market at Weicheng.
