translations.idiomatic: Then anonymous slander reached the throne; on the last day of the twelfth month he was ordered executed at Weicheng market.

context.previous: 或聞上無意殺嬰，復食，治病，議定不死矣。

translations.chinese: 春，蚡疾，一身盡痛，若有擊者，呼服謝罪。
translations.literal: In spring Fen fell ill; his whole body ached as if struck; he cried out that he submitted and begged pardon.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Tian Fen fell ill, racked with pains as from blows, screaming confessions and pleas for mercy.

context.next: 上使視鬼者瞻之，曰：「魏其侯與灌夫共守，笞欲殺之。」

translations.chinese: 上使視鬼者瞻之，曰：「魏其侯與灌夫共守，笞欲殺之。」
translations.literal: The emperor had one who could see ghosts examine him; he said, "Marquis of Weiqi and Guan Fu together guard him, beating him with sticks and wishing to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a spirit-medium, who reported, "Marquis Dou and Guan Fu stand over him, flogging him to death."

context.previous: 春，蚡疾，一身盡痛，若有擊者，呼服謝罪。
context.next: 竟死。

translations.chinese: 竟死。
translations.literal: In the end he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

context.previous: 上使視鬼者瞻之，曰：「魏其侯與灌夫共守，笞欲殺之。」
context.next: 子恬嗣，元朔中有罪免。

translations.chinese: 子恬嗣，元朔中有罪免。
translations.literal: His son Tian succeeded; during Yuanshuo he committed a crime and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tian inherited the title but lost it to a crime in Yuanshuo.

context.previous: 竟死。

translations.chinese: 後淮南王安謀反，覺。
translations.literal: Later the King of Huainan, Liu An, plotted rebellion; it was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu An, king of Huainan, rebelled; the plot was exposed.

context.next: 始安入朝時，蚡為太尉，迎安霸上，謂安曰：「上未有太子，大王最賢，高祖孫，即宮車晏駕，非大王立，尚誰立哉？」

translations.chinese: 始安入朝時，蚡為太尉，迎安霸上，謂安曰：「上未有太子，大王最賢，高祖孫，即宮車晏駕，非大王立，尚誰立哉？」
translations.literal: When An first entered court for an audience, Fen was grand commandant; he welcomed An at Bashang and said to An, "The emperor has not yet established an heir apparent; you, great king, are the worthiest, a grandson of Gaozu; when the imperial carriage is delayed in setting out, if not you, great king, who is established, who else could be?"
translations.idiomatic: On Liu An's first visit to court, Tian Fen—then grand commandant—met him at Bashang and said, "The throne has no heir; you are Gaozu's ablest grandson; when the emperor dies, if anyone mounts the throne but you, who should it be?"

context.previous: 後淮南王安謀反，覺。
context.next: 淮南王大喜，厚遺金錢財物。

translations.chinese: 淮南王大喜，厚遺金錢財物。
translations.literal: The King of Huainan was greatly pleased and richly presented gold, cash, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Huainan was delighted and showered him with gold and treasure.

context.previous: 始安入朝時，蚡為太尉，迎安霸上，謂安曰：「上未有太子，大王最賢，高祖孫，即宮車晏駕，非大王立，尚誰立哉？」
context.next: 上自嬰、夫事時不直蚡，特為太后故。

translations.chinese: 上自嬰、夫事時不直蚡，特為太后故。
translations.literal: From the time of the affair of Ying and Fu the emperor had not thought Fen in the right, but only for the empress dowager's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Dou–Guan affair the emperor had judged Tian Fen in the wrong but indulged him for his mother's sake.

context.previous: 淮南王大喜，厚遺金錢財物。
context.next: 及聞淮南事，上曰：「使武安侯在者，族矣。」

translations.chinese: 及聞淮南事，上曰：「使武安侯在者，族矣。」
translations.literal: When he heard of the Huainan affair, the emperor said, "If Marquis of Wu'an were still alive, he would have been exterminated to the clan."
translations.idiomatic: When the Huainan case broke, the emperor said, "If Tian Fen still lived, I would exterminate his whole line."

context.previous: 上自嬰、夫事時不直蚡，特為太后故。

translations.chinese: 韓安國
translations.literal: Han Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Han Anguo.

translations.chinese: 韓安國字長孺，梁成安人也，後徒睢陽。
translations.literal: Han Anguo, courtesy name Changru, was a man of Cheng'an in Liang; later he moved to Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo, courtesy name Changru, was a native of Cheng'an in Liang; his family later moved to Suiyang.

context.next: 嘗受《韓子》、雜說鄒田生所。

translations.chinese: 嘗受《韓子》、雜說鄒田生所。
translations.literal: He once studied the Han Feizi and miscellaneous doctrines under Zou Tiansheng of Zou.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied the Han Feizi and eclectic texts under Zou Tiansheng.

context.previous: 韓安國字長孺，梁成安人也，後徒睢陽。
context.next: 事梁孝王，為中大夫。

translations.chinese: 事梁孝王，為中大夫。
translations.literal: He served King Xiao of Liang as palace counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He served King Xiao of Liang as a palace counselor.

context.previous: 嘗受《韓子》、雜說鄒田生所。
context.next: 吳、楚反時，孝王使安國及張羽為將，扞吳兵於東界。

translations.chinese: 吳、楚反時，孝王使安國及張羽為將，扞吳兵於東界。
translations.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, King Xiao sent Anguo and Zhang Yu as generals to block the Wu army on the eastern border.
translations.idiomatic: During the revolt of Wu and Chu the king sent Han Anguo and Zhang Yu east to hold the Wu forces at the border.

context.previous: 事梁孝王，為中大夫。
context.next: 張羽力戰，安國持重，以故吳不能過梁。

translations.chinese: 張羽力戰，安國持重，以故吳不能過梁。
translations.literal: Zhang Yu fought hard; Anguo held steady; for this reason Wu could not pass Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu attacked fiercely; Han Anguo held the line; Wu never broke through into Liang.

context.previous: 吳、楚反時，孝王使安國及張羽為將，扞吳兵於東界。
context.next: 吳、楚破、安國、張羽名由此顯梁。

translations.chinese: 吳、楚破、安國、張羽名由此顯梁。
translations.literal: When Wu and Chu were defeated, Anguo and Zhang Yu's names from this became illustrious in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu and Chu fell, both men's fame shone in Liang.

context.previous: 張羽力戰，安國持重，以故吳不能過梁。

translations.chinese: 梁王以至親故，得自置相、二千石，出入遊戲，僭於天子。
translations.literal: Because the King of Liang was close kin, he was permitted to appoint his own chancellor and officials at two thousand piculs; in going out and coming in for sport he exceeded the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's brother, the king of Liang could name his own chancellor and two-thousand-picul officials; his comings and goings aped the imperial style.

context.next: 天子聞之，心不善。

translations.chinese: 天子聞之，心不善。
translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of it, his heart was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and took offense.

context.previous: 梁王以至親故，得自置相、二千石，出入遊戲，僭於天子。
context.next: 太后知帝弗善，乃怒梁使者，弗見，案責王所為。

translations.chinese: 太后知帝弗善，乃怒梁使者，弗見，案責王所為。
translations.literal: The empress dowager knew the emperor did not approve; she then grew angry at Liang's envoys, would not receive them, and investigated and called the king to account for his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager knew her son disapproved; she snubbed Liang's messengers and demanded an accounting of the king's behavior.

context.previous: 天子聞之，心不善。
context.next: 安國為梁使，見大長公主而泣曰：「何梁王為人子之孝，為人臣之忠，而太后曾不省也？

translations.chinese: 安國為梁使，見大長公主而泣曰：「何梁王為人子之孝，為人臣之忠，而太后曾不省也？
translations.literal: Anguo, as Liang's envoy, saw the grand princess and wept, saying, "How is it that the King of Liang, as a son, is filial, as a minister is loyal, yet the empress dowager never examines this?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo, speaking for Liang, wept before the grand princess: "The king is a dutiful son and a loyal vassal—why will the empress dowager not see it?"

context.previous: 太后知帝弗善，乃怒梁使者，弗見，案責王所為。
context.next: 夫前日吳、楚、齊、趙七國反，自關以東皆合從而西向，唯梁最親，為限難。

translations.chinese: 夫前日吳、楚、齊、趙七國反，自關以東皆合從而西向，唯梁最親，為限難。
translations.literal: "The other day when Wu, Chu, Qi, Zhao, and the seven states rebelled, from the passes east all joined in a vertical alliance and faced west; only Liang was closest kin and formed the hard barrier."
translations.idiomatic: "When the seven kingdoms rose east of the passes and turned their spears westward, only Liang—closest of kin—bore the brunt."

context.previous: 安國為梁使，見大長公主而泣曰：「何梁王為人子之孝，為人臣之忠，而太后曾不省也？
context.next: 梁王念太后、帝在中，而諸侯擾亂，壹言泣數行而下，跪送臣等六人將兵擊卻吳、楚、吳、楚以故兵不敢西，而卒破亡，梁之力也。

translations.chinese: 梁王念太后、帝在中，而諸侯擾亂，壹言泣數行而下，跪送臣等六人將兵擊卻吳、楚、吳、楚以故兵不敢西，而卒破亡，梁之力也。
translations.literal: "The King of Liang thought of the empress dowager and the emperor amid them while the marquises were in turmoil; with one word his tears fell in several streams; he knelt and sent us six men with troops to strike back Wu and Chu; for this reason Wu and Chu did not dare go west, and in the end were broken and destroyed—the strength was Liang's."
translations.idiomatic: "With the realm in chaos he thought only of you and the emperor; tears streamed at a single word; he knelt and sent six of us with an army that pinned Wu and Chu so they never marched west—that broke the rebellion."

context.previous: 夫前日吳、楚、齊、趙七國反，自關以東皆合從而西向，唯梁最親，為限難。
context.next: 今太后以小苛禮責望梁王。

translations.chinese: 今太后以小苛禮責望梁王。
translations.literal: "Now the empress dowager blames and expects the King of Liang over petty matters of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: "Now you fault him for petty breaches of etiquette."

context.previous: 梁王念太后、帝在中，而諸侯擾亂，壹言泣數行而下，跪送臣等六人將兵擊卻吳、楚、吳、楚以故兵不敢西，而卒破亡，梁之力也。
context.next: 梁王父兄皆帝王，而所見者大，故出稱蹕，入言警，車旗皆帝所賜，即以□鄙小縣，驅馳國中，欲誇諸侯，令天下知太后、帝愛之也。

translations.chinese: 梁王父兄皆帝王，而所見者大，故出稱蹕，入言警，車旗皆帝所賜，即以□鄙小縣，驅馳國中，欲誇諸侯，令天下知太后、帝愛之也。
translations.literal: "The King of Liang's father and elder brothers were all emperors, and what he has seen is great; therefore when he goes out he speaks of clearing the way, when he enters he speaks of precautions; chariots and banners were all gifts from the emperor—even in this petty commandery he gallops through the state, wishing to boast to the marquises and let the realm know the empress dowager and the emperor love him."
translations.idiomatic: "Raised among emperors, he thinks in large scale: he speaks of imperial escort and cordons because his equipage was all your gift; even on a tour of a minor county he parades the kingdom so all may see how you and the emperor cherish him."

context.previous: 今太后以小苛禮責望梁王。
context.next: 今梁使來，輒案責之，梁王恐，日夜滋泣思慕，不知所為。

translations.chinese: 今梁使來，輒案責之，梁王恐，日夜滋泣思慕，不知所為。
translations.literal: "Now whenever Liang's envoys come, you always investigate and call them to account; the King of Liang is afraid, day and night weeps and longs in thought, and does not know what to do."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet every Liang messenger is hauled in for interrogation; the king lives in terror, weeping day and night, unsure what to do."

context.previous: 梁王父兄皆帝王，而所見者大，故出稱蹕，入言警，車旗皆帝所賜，即以□鄙小縣，驅馳國中，欲誇諸侯，令天下知太后、帝愛之也。
context.next: 何梁王之忠孝而太后不恤也？」

translations.chinese: 何梁王之忠孝而太后不恤也？」
translations.literal: "How can the King of Liang be loyal and filial while the empress dowager shows no pity?"
translations.idiomatic: "How can he be so loyal and filial while you withhold your mercy?"

context.previous: 今梁使來，輒案責之，梁王恐，日夜滋泣思慕，不知所為。
context.next: 長公主具以告太后，太后喜曰：「為帝言之。」

translations.chinese: 長公主具以告太后，太后喜曰：「為帝言之。」
translations.literal: The grand princess reported everything to the empress dowager; the empress dowager was pleased and said, "Speak of it to the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The grand princess repeated every word; the empress dowager beamed and said, "Tell the emperor."

context.previous: 何梁王之忠孝而太后不恤也？」
context.next: 言之，帝心乃解，而免冠謝太后曰：「兄弟不能相教，乃為太后遺憂。」

translations.chinese: 言之，帝心乃解，而免冠謝太后曰：「兄弟不能相教，乃為太后遺憂。」
translations.literal: When she spoke of it, the emperor's heart was then relieved; he removed his cap and apologized to the empress dowager, saying, "Brothers could not instruct each other, and so caused the empress dowager worry."
translations.idiomatic: She did; the emperor's anger melted. He doffed his cap and apologized to his mother: "We brothers failed each other and caused you grief."

context.previous: 長公主具以告太后，太后喜曰：「為帝言之。」
context.next: 悉見梁使，厚賜之。

translations.chinese: 悉見梁使，厚賜之。
translations.literal: He received all Liang's envoys and richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: He received every Liang envoy and rewarded them generously.

context.previous: 言之，帝心乃解，而免冠謝太后曰：「兄弟不能相教，乃為太后遺憂。」
context.next: 其後，梁王益親歡。

translations.chinese: 其後，梁王益親歡。
translations.literal: After that, the King of Liang grew ever closer in affection.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the bond between throne and king of Liang grew warm again.

context.previous: 悉見梁使，厚賜之。
context.next: 太后、長公主更賜安國直千餘金。

translations.chinese: 太后、長公主更賜安國直千餘金。
translations.literal: The empress dowager and the grand princess additionally bestowed on Anguo more than a thousand in cash weight of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and the grand princess together gave Han Anguo over a thousand cash-weight in gold.

context.previous: 其後，梁王益親歡。
context.next: 由此顯，結於漢。

translations.chinese: 由此顯，結於漢。
translations.literal: From this he became eminent and formed ties with Han.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in fame and was tied to the court at Chang'an.

context.previous: 太后、長公主更賜安國直千餘金。

translations.chinese: 其後，安國坐法抵罪，蒙獄吏田申辱安國。
translations.literal: Later Anguo committed a crime under the law and paid the penalty; the clerk Tian Jia of Meng prison humiliated Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Anguo broke the law and went to prison, where the warder Tian Jia abused him.

context.next: 安國曰：「死灰獨不復然乎？」

translations.chinese: 安國曰：「死灰獨不復然乎？」
translations.literal: Anguo said, "Does dead ash alone never blaze again?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said, "Dead embers cannot reignite—or can they?"

context.previous: 其後，安國坐法抵罪，蒙獄吏田申辱安國。
context.next: 甲曰：「然即溺之。」

translations.chinese: 甲曰：「然即溺之。」
translations.literal: Jia said, "If it blazes I will urinate on it."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jia sneered, "If they do, I will piss them out."

context.previous: 安國曰：「死灰獨不復然乎？」
context.next: 居無幾，梁內史缺，漢使使者拜安國為梁內史，起徒中為二千石。

translations.chinese: 居無幾，梁內史缺，漢使使者拜安國為梁內史，起徒中為二千石。
translations.literal: Before long the post of inner secretary was vacant; Han sent an envoy to appoint Anguo inner secretary of Liang, raising him from the convicts' ranks to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the post of Liang's inner secretary fell vacant; the court appointed Han Anguo from his cell straight to two-thousand-picul rank.

context.previous: 甲曰：「然即溺之。」
context.next: 田甲亡。

translations.chinese: 田甲亡。
translations.literal: Tian Jia fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jia ran.

context.previous: 居無幾，梁內史缺，漢使使者拜安國為梁內史，起徒中為二千石。
context.next: 安國曰：「甲不就官，我滅而宗。」

translations.chinese: 安國曰：「甲不就官，我滅而宗。」
translations.literal: Anguo said, "If Jia does not take office, I will exterminate his clan."
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo sent word: "If Tian Jia does not show up for duty, I will wipe out his family."

context.previous: 田甲亡。
context.next: 甲肉袒謝，安國笑曰：「公等足與治乎？」

translations.chinese: 甲肉袒謝，安國笑曰：「公等足與治乎？」
translations.literal: Jia bared his shoulder and apologized; Anguo laughed and said, "Are you gentlemen enough to be worth dealing with?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jia stripped to the waist and crawled to apologize. Han Anguo laughed: "Were you worth the trouble?"

context.previous: 安國曰：「甲不就官，我滅而宗。」
context.next: 卒善遇之。

translations.chinese: 卒善遇之。
translations.literal: In the end he treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he treated him kindly.

context.previous: 甲肉袒謝，安國笑曰：「公等足與治乎？」

translations.chinese: 內史之缺也，王新得齊人公孫詭，說之，欲請為內史。
translations.literal: When the inner secretary post was vacant, the king had newly obtained the Qi man Gongsun Gui, was pleased with him, and wished to request him as inner secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the post opened, the king favored a newcomer from Qi, Gongsun Gui, and meant to name him inner secretary.

context.next: 竇太后聞，乃詔王以安國為內史。

translations.chinese: 竇太后聞，乃詔王以安國為內史。
translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Dou heard, she then issued an edict to the king to appoint Anguo as inner secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Dou heard and ordered the king to appoint Han Anguo instead.

context.previous: 內史之缺也，王新得齊人公孫詭，說之，欲請為內史。

translations.chinese: 公孫詭、羊勝說王求為帝太子及益地事，恐漢大臣不聽，乃陰使人刺漢用事謀臣。
translations.literal: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng persuaded the king to seek to become heir apparent to the emperor and to increase his territory; fearing Han ministers would not consent, they secretly sent men to assassinate influential Han strategists.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng urged the king to seek the crown princeship and more land; fearing refusal from Chang'an, they hired killers for Han's leading advisers.

context.next: 及殺故吳相爰盎，景帝遂聞詭、勝等計劃，乃遣使捕詭、勝，必得。

translations.chinese: 及殺故吳相爰盎，景帝遂聞詭、勝等計劃，乃遣使捕詭、勝，必得。
translations.literal: When they had killed the former chancellor of Wu, Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing eventually learned of Gui and Sheng's plots; he then sent agents to arrest Gui and Sheng, demanding they be taken.
translations.idiomatic: After they murdered Yuan Ang, the former chancellor of Wu, Emperor Jing learned of the plot and sent men to seize Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng alive.

context.previous: 公孫詭、羊勝說王求為帝太子及益地事，恐漢大臣不聽，乃陰使人刺漢用事謀臣。
context.next: 漢使十輩至梁，相以下舉國大索，月餘弗得。

translations.chinese: 漢使十輩至梁，相以下舉國大索，月餘弗得。
translations.literal: Han envoys came in ten parties to Liang; from the chancellor down the whole state searched greatly for more than a month without finding them.
translations.idiomatic: Ten separate Han delegations searched Liang from chancellor to constable for over a month without success.

context.previous: 及殺故吳相爰盎，景帝遂聞詭、勝等計劃，乃遣使捕詭、勝，必得。
context.next: 安國聞詭、勝匿王所，乃入見王而泣曰：「主辱者臣死。

translations.chinese: 安國聞詭、勝匿王所，乃入見王而泣曰：「主辱者臣死。
translations.literal: Anguo heard that Gui and Sheng were hidden at the king's place; he then entered, saw the king, and wept, saying, "When the ruler is shamed, the minister should die."
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo learned the two men were hidden in the palace. He entered in tears: "When the lord is dishonored, his servant should die."

context.previous: 漢使十輩至梁，相以下舉國大索，月餘弗得。
context.next: 大王無良臣，故紛紛至此。

translations.chinese: 大王無良臣，故紛紛至此。
translations.literal: "The great king has no good ministers; therefore it has come to this confusion."
translations.idiomatic: "You have no loyal ministers—that is why matters have come to this pass."

context.previous: 安國聞詭、勝匿王所，乃入見王而泣曰：「主辱者臣死。
context.next: 今勝、詭不得，請辭賜死。」

translations.chinese: 今勝、詭不得，請辭賜死。」
translations.literal: "Now that Sheng and Gui cannot be obtained, I beg leave to accept a gift of death."
translations.idiomatic: "If those two are not produced, grant me death."

context.previous: 大王無良臣，故紛紛至此。
context.next: 王曰：「何至此？」

translations.chinese: 王曰：「何至此？」
translations.literal: The king said, "How has it reached this?"
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "How can it be so grave?"

context.previous: 今勝、詭不得，請辭賜死。」
context.next: 安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與太上皇之與高帝及皇帝與臨江王親？」

translations.chinese: 安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與太上皇之與高帝及皇帝與臨江王親？」
translations.literal: Anguo's tears fell in several streams as he said, "Great king, you yourself measure against the emperor—which is closer, the Grand Supreme Emperor to Gaozu, or the emperor to the Prince of Linjiang?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo wept freely: "Tell me—which bond is tighter: the Grand Supreme Emperor and Gaozu, or the emperor and the prince of Linjiang?"

context.previous: 王曰：「何至此？」
context.next: 王曰：「弗如也。」

translations.chinese: 王曰：「弗如也。」
translations.literal: The king said, "It does not compare."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "I am not as close to the emperor as those pairs were."

context.previous: 安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與太上皇之與高帝及皇帝與臨江王親？」
context.next: 安國曰：「夫太上皇、臨江親父子間，然高帝曰『提三尺取天下者朕也』，故太上終不得制事，居於櫟陽。

translations.chinese: 安國曰：「夫太上皇、臨江親父子間，然高帝曰『提三尺取天下者朕也』，故太上終不得制事，居於櫟陽。
translations.literal: Anguo said, "Between the Grand Supreme Emperor and Gaozu, and between the Prince of Linjiang and the emperor—these were close father-and-son bonds—yet Gaozu said, 'He who took the realm with a three-foot sword is I,' so in the end the Grand Supreme could not control affairs and dwelt at Liyang."
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said: "Gaozu and his father, the emperor and the prince of Linjiang—each was a tight father-son pair—yet Gaozu declared, The sword that won the realm is mine, and the old emperor finished his life powerless at Liyang."

context.previous: 王曰：「弗如也。」
context.next: 臨江，適長太子，以一言過，廢王臨江；

translations.chinese: 臨江，適長太子，以一言過，廢王臨江；
translations.literal: Linjiang, as the eldest heir apparent of the proper line, because of one word's fault was deposed as king of Linjiang;
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Linjiang was the legitimate eldest son; one slip of the tongue cost him his kingdom;

context.previous: 安國曰：「夫太上皇、臨江親父子間，然高帝曰『提三尺取天下者朕也』，故太上終不得制事，居於櫟陽。
context.next: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。

translations.chinese: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。
translations.literal: because of the affair of the palace walls, in the end he killed himself in the commandant of the capital's office.
translations.idiomatic: on a charge about palace walls he ended his life in the metropolitan commandant's yamen.

context.previous: 臨江，適長太子，以一言過，廢王臨江；
context.next: 何者？

translations.chinese: 何者？
translations.literal: Why was it so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

context.previous: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。
context.next: 治天下終不用私亂公。

translations.chinese: 治天下終不用私亂公。
translations.literal: In ruling the realm one never uses private feeling to disorder the public good.
translations.idiomatic: Because the empire is never ruled by private affection over public law.

context.previous: 何者？
context.next: 語曰：『雖有親父，安知不為虎？

translations.chinese: 語曰：『雖有親父，安知不為虎？
translations.literal: The saying goes, "Though there is a loving father, how do you know he is not a tiger?"
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: Even a loving father may prove a tiger;

context.previous: 治天下終不用私亂公。
context.next: 雖有親兄，安知不為狼？』

translations.chinese: 雖有親兄，安知不為狼？』
translations.literal: "Though there is a loving elder brother, how do you know he is not a wolf?"
translations.idiomatic: even a loving brother may prove a wolf."

context.previous: 語曰：『雖有親父，安知不為虎？
context.next: 今大王列在諸侯，訹邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。

translations.chinese: 今大王列在諸侯，訹邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。
translations.literal: "Now you, great king, are listed among the marquises; seduced by wicked ministers' empty talk, you violate the sovereign's prohibitions and bend the clear law."
translations.idiomatic: "You are only a feudal king; venal advisers have led you to break the throne's edicts and warp the code."

context.previous: 雖有親兄，安知不為狼？』
context.next: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於大王。

translations.chinese: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於大王。
translations.literal: "The Son of Heaven, for the empress dowager's sake, cannot bear to apply the law to you, great king."
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor stays his hand only for his mother's sake."

context.previous: 今大王列在諸侯，訹邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。
context.next: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，大王終不覺寤。

translations.chinese: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，大王終不覺寤。
translations.literal: "The empress dowager weeps day and night, hoping you, great king, will reform yourself; you, great king, never wake to it."
translations.idiomatic: "She weeps day and night for you to mend your ways; you refuse to wake."

context.previous: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於大王。
context.next: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？」

translations.chinese: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？」
translations.literal: "Suppose the empress dowager's carriage should be delayed in setting out—whom will you, great king, cling to then?"
translations.idiomatic: "When her carriage at last climbs the western slope, whom will you cling to?"

context.previous: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，大王終不覺寤。
context.next: 語未卒，王泣數行而下，謝安國曰：「吾今出之。」

translations.chinese: 語未卒，王泣數行而下，謝安國曰：「吾今出之。」
translations.literal: Before the words were finished, the king's tears fell in several streams; he apologized to Anguo, saying, "I will now release them."
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the king was sobbing; he thanked Han Anguo and said, "I will hand them over."

context.previous: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？」
context.next: 即日詭、勝自殺。

translations.chinese: 即日詭、勝自殺。
translations.literal: That same day Gui and Sheng killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: That day Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng committed suicide.

context.previous: 語未卒，王泣數行而下，謝安國曰：「吾今出之。」
context.next: 漢使還報，梁事皆得釋，安國力也。

translations.chinese: 漢使還報，梁事皆得釋，安國力也。
translations.literal: The Han envoy returned and reported; the Liang affair was all released—it was Anguo's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Han envoy reported back; the Liang crisis dissolved—through Han Anguo's doing.

context.previous: 即日詭、勝自殺。
context.next: 景帝、太后益重安國。

translations.chinese: 景帝、太后益重安國。
translations.literal: Emperor Jing and the empress dowager valued Anguo all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing and the empress dowager prized him the more.

context.previous: 漢使還報，梁事皆得釋，安國力也。

translations.chinese: 孝王薨，共王即位，安國坐法失官，家居。
translations.literal: When King Xiao died, King Gong ascended; Anguo committed a crime under the law and lost his office, living at home.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xiao died and King Gong succeeded, Han Anguo lost his post to a legal offense and lived in retirement.

context.next: 武帝即位，武安侯田蚡為太尉，親貴用事。

translations.chinese: 武帝即位，武安侯田蚡為太尉，親貴用事。
translations.literal: When Emperor Wu mounted the throne, Marquis of Wu'an Tian Fen was grand commandant, close and noble and wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Marquis of Wu'an Tian Fen was grand commandant, powerful and the emperor's favorite.

context.previous: 孝王薨，共王即位，安國坐法失官，家居。
context.next: 安國以五百金遺蚡，蚡言安國太后，上素聞安國賢，即召以為北地都尉，遷為大司農。

translations.chinese: 安國以五百金遺蚡，蚡言安國太后，上素聞安國賢，即召以為北地都尉，遷為大司農。
translations.literal: Anguo presented five hundred in gold weight to Fen; Fen spoke of Anguo to the empress dowager; the emperor had long heard Anguo was worthy; he immediately summoned him to be commandant of Beidi, then promoted him to minister of finance.
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo gave Tian Fen five hundred catties of gold; Tian Fen praised him to the empress dowager; the emperor, who had long heard of his talent, named him commandant of Beidi, then minister of finance.

context.previous: 武帝即位，武安侯田蚡為太尉，親貴用事。
context.next: 閩、東越相攻，遣安國、大行王恢將兵。

translations.chinese: 閩、東越相攻，遣安國、大行王恢將兵。
translations.literal: Min and Eastern Yue attacked each other; he sent Anguo and Grand Coach Wang Hui with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Min and Eastern Yue went to war, the court sent Han Anguo and Grand Coach Wang Hui with an army.

context.previous: 安國以五百金遺蚡，蚡言安國太后，上素聞安國賢，即召以為北地都尉，遷為大司農。
context.next: 未至越，越殺其王降，漢兵亦罷。

translations.chinese: 未至越，越殺其王降，漢兵亦罷。

translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived the Yue people killed their king and submitted; the Han force was dismissed.

translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said, "A campaign a thousand li from home rarely ends in clear victory."

translations.literal: "Now the Xiongnu rely on the sufficiency of their war horses, harbor the hearts of birds and beasts, move like birds flocking—they are hard to catch and control."
translations.idiomatic: "The nomads ride as long as their horses hold out, think like beasts, scatter and regather like birds—nearly impossible to pin down."

translations.chinese: 得其地不足為廣，有其眾不足為強，自上古弗屬。
translations.literal: "To gain their land is not enough to be called vast; to possess their multitudes is not enough to be called strong; from high antiquity they have not belonged to us."
translations.idiomatic: "Their land would not widen the empire; their herds would not strengthen it; they have never been true subjects since high antiquity."

translations.literal: If Han contends for gain over several thousand li, then men and horses will be exhausted; the barbarians, with their forces intact, will exploit our weakness—the situation is sure to be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Drive thousands of li for plunder and you exhaust men and horses; the nomads wait at full strength to strike your weakness—a recipe for disaster.

translations.literal: The next year Nie Yi, a magnate of Mayi in Yanmen, spoke through Grand Coach Wang Hui: "The Xiongnu have newly made peace through marriage alliance and trust the border; they can be lured with profit to come; ambush troops and strike them—it is the way surely to break them."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Nie Yi of Mayi in Yanmen, speaking through Grand Coach Wang Hui, said: "The Xiongnu have just sealed a heqin and trust the frontier; bait them with loot, then spring an ambush—that will break them."

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned the dukes and ministers and asked, "I have adorned my daughters to match the shanyu; silks and patterned brocade, bribing him very richly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers: "I have married imperial daughters to the shanyu and sent treasure in silks and brocades beyond measure."

translations.chinese: 單于待命加嫚，侵盜無已，邊竟數驚，朕甚閔之。
translations.literal: The shanyu has awaited commands only to add arrogance; raiding and plundering without end, the border has repeatedly been alarmed—I am greatly pained by it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he answers every favor with contempt, raids without end, and keeps the frontier in panic—I cannot bear it."

translations.literal: "Now I wish to raise troops to attack them—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: "Shall we strike him with an army?"

context.previous: 單于待命加嫚，侵盜無已，邊竟數驚，朕甚閔之。

translations.chinese: 大行恢對曰：「陛下雖未言，臣固願效之。
translations.literal: Grand Coach Hui replied, "Though Your Majesty has not yet spoken, your servant has long wished to offer this."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui said, "Even if you had not asked, I would have urged the same."

context.next: 臣聞全代之時，北有強胡之敵，內連中國之兵，然尚得養老長幼，種樹以時，倉廩常實，匈奴不輕侵也。

translations.chinese: 臣聞全代之時，北有強胡之敵，內連中國之兵，然尚得養老長幼，種樹以時，倉廩常實，匈奴不輕侵也。
translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that in the integrity of Dai, though there was a strong Hu enemy to the north and troops of the central states linked within, they were still able to nurture the old and raise the young, plant trees in season, and the granaries were always full—the Xiongnu did not lightly invade."
translations.idiomatic: "In the old state of Dai, hemmed by the nomads within and imperial armies without, the people still raised children, sowed on time, and filled their granaries—because the Xiongnu did not dare raid lightly."

context.previous: 大行恢對曰：「陛下雖未言，臣固願效之。
context.next: 今以陛下之威，海內為一，天下同任，又遣子弟乘邊守塞，轉粟挽輸，以為之備，然匈奴侵盜不已者，無它，以不恐之故耳。

translations.chinese: 今以陛下之威，海內為一，天下同任，又遣子弟乘邊守塞，轉粟挽輸，以為之備，然匈奴侵盜不已者，無它，以不恐之故耳。
translations.literal: "Now with Your Majesty's majesty, within the seas unified, the realm sharing the burden, moreover dispatching sons and younger brothers to ride the border and guard the passes, carting grain and hauling supplies to prepare for them—yet the Xiongnu raid and plunder without cease; there is no other reason than that they are not afraid."
translations.idiomatic: "Today, under your majesty, the empire is one, the people shoulder the cost, your kin ride the walls, grain trains feed the garrisons—and still the Xiongnu raid. There is only one reason: they no longer fear us."

context.previous: 臣聞全代之時，北有強胡之敵，內連中國之兵，然尚得養老長幼，種樹以時，倉廩常實，匈奴不輕侵也。

translations.literal: "Your servant privately holds that striking them is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: "Strike them—that is my counsel."

translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said, "No."

translations.chinese: 臣聞高皇帝嘗圍於平城，匈奴至者投鞍高如城者數所。
translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that the High Emperor was once surrounded at Pingcheng; the Xiongnu who arrived stacked saddles in several places as high as a wall."
translations.idiomatic: "Gaozu was trapped at Pingcheng; the nomads piled captured saddles like ramparts around him."

context.previous: 御史大夫安國曰：「不然。
context.next: 平城之饑，七日不食，天下歌之，及解圍反位，而無忿怒之心。

translations.chinese: 平城之饑，七日不食，天下歌之，及解圍反位，而無忿怒之心。
translations.literal: "The hunger at Pingcheng—seven days without food; the realm sang of it; yet when the siege lifted and he returned to the throne, he bore no heart of rage."
translations.idiomatic: "Seven days without food—the whole empire remembers—yet when the ring broke and he resumed the throne, he nursed no private vengeance."

context.previous: 臣聞高皇帝嘗圍於平城，匈奴至者投鞍高如城者數所。
context.next: 夫聖人以天下為度者也，不以己私怒傷天下之功，故乃遣劉敬奉金千斤，以結和親，至今為五世利。

translations.chinese: 夫聖人以天下為度者也，不以己私怒傷天下之功，故乃遣劉敬奉金千斤，以結和親，至今為五世利。
translations.literal: "A sage takes the realm as his measure; he does not wound the work of the realm for private anger; therefore he sent Liu Jing with a thousand catties of gold to knot peace through marriage alliance—down to today it has benefited five generations."
translations.idiomatic: "A sage weighs the world, not his temper; he sent Liu Jing with a thousand catties of gold to seal a heqin—and five reigns have profited from it."

context.previous: 平城之饑，七日不食，天下歌之，及解圍反位，而無忿怒之心。
context.next: 孝文皇帝又嘗壹擁天下之精兵聚之廣武常溪，然終無尺寸之功，而天下黔首無不憂者。

translations.chinese: 孝文皇帝又嘗壹擁天下之精兵聚之廣武常溪，然終無尺寸之功，而天下黔首無不憂者。
translations.literal: "Emperor Wen once gathered the pick of the realm's troops at Guangwu and Changxi, yet in the end achieved not an inch of merit, while the black-haired commoners of the realm had none who were not anxious."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Wen once massed the empire's best troops at Guangwu and Changxi and won not a foot of ground, while every commoner lived in dread."

context.previous: 夫聖人以天下為度者也，不以己私怒傷天下之功，故乃遣劉敬奉金千斤，以結和親，至今為五世利。

translations.chinese: 孝文寤於兵之不可宿，故復合和親之約。
translations.literal: "Emperor Wen awoke to the truth that troops cannot be long stationed; therefore he renewed the covenant of peace through marriage alliance."
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Wen saw that armies cannot camp forever; he renewed the heqin compact."

context.previous: 孝文皇帝又嘗壹擁天下之精兵聚之廣武常溪，然終無尺寸之功，而天下黔首無不憂者。

translations.chinese: 此二聖之跡，足以為效矣。
translations.literal: "The tracks of these two sages are enough to serve as a model."
translations.idiomatic: "Those two sage emperors left us the model."

translations.idiomatic: "Do not strike—that is my counsel."

translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui said, "Wrong."

context.next: 臣聞五帝不相襲禮，三王不相復樂，非故相反也，各因世宜也。

translations.chinese: 臣聞五帝不相襲禮，三王不相復樂，非故相反也，各因世宜也。
translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that the Five Emperors did not inherit one another's ritual, the Three Kings did not repeat one another's music—not that they deliberately opposed each other, but each followed what suited the age."
translations.idiomatic: "The Five Emperors did not copy one another's rites, the Three Kings did not recycle one another's music—not from perversity, but because each age needs its own policy."

translations.chinese: 且高帝身被堅執銳，蒙霧露，沐霜雪，行幾十年，所以不報平城之怨者，非力不能，所以休天下之心也。
translations.literal: "Moreover the High Emperor personally wore hard armor and grasped sharp weapons, braved fog and dew, bathed in frost and snow, marched for nearly ten years; the reason he did not avenge the resentment of Pingcheng was not inability of strength—it was to rest the heart of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: "Gaozu marched ten years in mail and frost; he did not avenge Pingcheng because he could not, but because the realm needed peace."

context.previous: 臣聞五帝不相襲禮，三王不相復樂，非故相反也，各因世宜也。

translations.chinese: 今邊竟數驚，士卒傷死，中國槥車相望，此仁人之所隱也。
translations.literal: "Now the border is repeatedly alarmed, soldiers are wounded and die, and in the central states biers for the dead stand end to end along the roads—this is what a humane man would pity."
translations.idiomatic: "Today the frontier alarms never stop, soldiers fall, and funeral carts choke the roads of China—any humane ruler would pity that."

context.previous: 且高帝身被堅執銳，蒙霧露，沐霜雪，行幾十年，所以不報平城之怨者，非力不能，所以休天下之心也。

translations.literal: "Your servant therefore says, 'Striking is advantageous.'"
translations.idiomatic: "So I say: strike."

translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said again, "No."

context.next: 臣聞利不十者不易業，功不百者不變常，是以古之人君謀事必就祖，發政占古語，重作事也。

translations.chinese: 臣聞利不十者不易業，功不百者不變常，是以古之人君謀事必就祖，發政占古語，重作事也。
translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that if the gain is not tenfold one does not change occupation, if the merit is not hundredfold one does not alter the constant—therefore the rulers of antiquity, when planning affairs, always consulted the ancestors; when issuing policies they divined by ancient sayings, because they took changing course seriously."
translations.idiomatic: "Without tenfold gain men do not change trade; without hundredfold merit sages do not break precedent—ancient kings consulted shrines and oracles before they shifted policy."

context.previous: 安國曰：「不然。
context.next: 且自三代之盛，夷狄不與正朔服色，非威不能制，強弗能服也，以為遠方絕地不牧之民，不足煩中國也。

translations.chinese: 且自三代之盛，夷狄不與正朔服色，非威不能制，強弗能服也，以為遠方絕地不牧之民，不足煩中國也。
translations.literal: "Moreover since the height of the Three Dynasties, the Yi and Di have not shared the correct calendar and dress colors—not because might could not control them or strength could not subdue them, but because they were thought distant peoples beyond the pale, not worth troubling the central states."
translations.idiomatic: "Even at the height of the Three Dynasties the barbarians kept their own calendar and dress—not because China could not force them, but because they were deemed beyond the pale, unworthy of the empire's exertion."

context.previous: 臣聞利不十者不易業，功不百者不變常，是以古之人君謀事必就祖，發政占古語，重作事也。

translations.chinese: 且匈奴，輕疾悍亟之兵也，至如□風，去如收電，畜牧為業，弧弓射獵，逐獸隨草，居處無常，難得而制。
translations.literal: "Moreover the Xiongnu are troops light, swift, fierce, and sudden; they arrive like whirlwind, depart like gathered lightning; herding is their occupation, they bend the bow to hunt, follow the beasts and the grass, their dwelling places are not constant—they are hard to catch and control."
translations.idiomatic: "The Xiongnu strike like a squall and vanish like lightning; they live by the herd and the bow, follow grass and game, and never camp twice in the same place—nearly impossible to hold."

context.previous: 且自三代之盛，夷狄不與正朔服色，非威不能制，強弗能服也，以為遠方絕地不牧之民，不足煩中國也。

translations.chinese: 今使邊郡久廢耕織，以支胡之常事，其勢不相權也。
translations.literal: "Now to make the border commanderies long abandon plowing and weaving in order to sustain the Xiongnu's constant raids—their situations are not matched in power."
translations.idiomatic: "To idle the border farms and looms forever answering nomad raids is a fight we cannot sustain."

context.previous: 且匈奴，輕疾悍亟之兵也，至如□風，去如收電，畜牧為業，弧弓射獵，逐獸隨草，居處無常，難得而制。

translations.chinese: 臣聞鳳鳥乘於風，聖人因於時。
translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that the phoenix rides the wind, the sage rides the season."
translations.idiomatic: "The phoenix rides the wind; the sage rides the moment."

context.previous: 恢曰：「不然。
context.next: 昔秦繆公都雍，地方三百里，知時宜之變，攻取西戎，辟地千里，並國十四，隴西、北地是也。

translations.chinese: 昔秦繆公都雍，地方三百里，知時宜之變，攻取西戎，辟地千里，並國十四，隴西、北地是也。
translations.literal: "In the past Duke Mu of Qin made his capital at Yong; the territory was three hundred li square; knowing the changes suited to the times, he attacked and took the western Rong, opened a thousand li of land, annexed fourteen states—Longxi and Beidi are those."
translations.idiomatic: "Duke Mu of Qin ruled from Yong in a square three hundred li to a side; reading the times, he conquered the western Rong, opened a thousand li, swallowed fourteen states—Longxi and Beidi among them."

context.previous: 臣聞鳳鳥乘於風，聖人因於時。
context.next: 及後蒙恬為秦侵胡，辟數千里，以河為竟，累石為城，樹榆為塞，匈奴不敢飲馬於河，置烽燧然後敢牧馬。

translations.chinese: 及後蒙恬為秦侵胡，辟數千里，以河為竟，累石為城，樹榆為塞，匈奴不敢飲馬於河，置烽燧然後敢牧馬。
translations.literal: "Later Meng Tian for Qin invaded the Hu, opened several thousand li, took the Yellow River as the border, piled stone for walls, planted elms for palisades; the Xiongnu did not dare water their horses in the river; they set beacon fires only then dared pasture horses."
translations.idiomatic: "Meng Tian later drove the Hu for Qin, pushed the line to the Yellow River, raised stone walls and elm palisades; the Xiongnu would not water horses in the river until their watchfires lined the steppe."

context.previous: 昔秦繆公都雍，地方三百里，知時宜之變，攻取西戎，辟地千里，並國十四，隴西、北地是也。
context.next: 夫匈奴獨可以威服，不可以仁畜也。

translations.chinese: 夫匈奴獨可以威服，不可以仁畜也。
translations.literal: "The Xiongnu can be subdued by might alone; they cannot be nurtured by benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: "Fear alone governs the Xiongnu; kindness does not tame them."

context.previous: 及後蒙恬為秦侵胡，辟數千里，以河為竟，累石為城，樹榆為塞，匈奴不敢飲馬於河，置烽燧然後敢牧馬。
context.next: 今以中國之盛，萬倍之資，遣百分之一以攻匈奴，譬猶以強弩射且潰之癰也，必不留行矣。

translations.chinese: 今以中國之盛，萬倍之資，遣百分之一以攻匈奴，譬猶以強弩射且潰之癰也，必不留行矣。
translations.literal: "Now with the flourishing of the central states, with resources ten thousand times as great, to dispatch one hundredth of them to attack the Xiongnu is like shooting a ripe, bursting boil with a powerful crossbow—it is sure not to stick in the going."
translations.idiomatic: "China today is rich beyond measure; spend one percent of that on a campaign and it is like a heavy crossbow bolt through a ripe boil—it will not stall halfway."

context.previous: 夫匈奴獨可以威服，不可以仁畜也。
context.next: 若是，則北發月氏可得而臣也。

translations.chinese: 若是，則北發月氏可得而臣也。
translations.literal: "If so, then even summoning the Yuezhi from the north can be got and made to serve."
translations.idiomatic: "Success would let us bring even the Yuezhi to heel in the north."

context.previous: 今以中國之盛，萬倍之資，遣百分之一以攻匈奴，譬猶以強弩射且潰之癰也，必不留行矣。
context.next: 臣故曰『擊之便』。」

translations.chinese: 臣故曰『擊之便』。」
translations.literal: "Your servant therefore says, 'Striking is advantageous.'"
translations.idiomatic: "So I say: strike."

context.previous: 若是，則北發月氏可得而臣也。

translations.chinese: 安國曰：「不然。
translations.literal: Anguo said, "It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo said again, "No."

context.next: 臣聞用兵者以飽待饑，正治以待其亂，定捨以待其勞。

translations.chinese: 臣聞用兵者以飽待饑，正治以待其亂，定捨以待其勞。
translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that one who uses troops waits with full bellies for hunger, waits with upright rule for their disorder, waits with settled camp for their fatigue."
translations.idiomatic: "The art of war is to meet hunger with full stores, chaos with order, exhaustion with rested troops."

context.previous: 安國曰：「不然。
context.next: 故接兵覆眾，伐國墮城，常坐而役敵國，此聖人之兵也。

translations.chinese: 故接兵覆眾，伐國墮城，常坐而役敵國，此聖人之兵也。
translations.literal: "Therefore to join battle and overturn hosts, attack states and cast down cities, often sitting still while wearing down the enemy state—this is the army of the sages."
translations.idiomatic: "To shatter armies and take cities while the enemy exhausts itself—that is the sage general's way."

context.previous: 臣聞用兵者以飽待饑，正治以待其亂，定捨以待其勞。
context.next: 且臣聞之，沖風之衰，不能起毛羽；

translations.chinese: 且臣聞之，沖風之衰，不能起毛羽；
translations.literal: "Moreover your servant has heard that a dying gust cannot lift a feather;"
translations.idiomatic: "A dying gust cannot lift a feather;"

context.previous: 故接兵覆眾，伐國墮城，常坐而役敵國，此聖人之兵也。
context.next: 強弩之末，力不能入魯縞。

translations.chinese: 強弩之末，力不能入魯縞。
translations.literal: "at the end of a strong crossbow's shot, the force cannot pierce Lu silk."
translations.idiomatic: "a spent crossbow cannot pierce thin Lu gauze."

context.previous: 且臣聞之，沖風之衰，不能起毛羽；
context.next: 夫盛之有衰，猶朝之必莫也。

translations.chinese: 夫盛之有衰，猶朝之必莫也。
translations.literal: "That flourishing has decline is like morning having evening."
translations.idiomatic: "Strength always wanes, as morning turns to evening."

context.previous: 強弩之末，力不能入魯縞。
context.next: 今將卷甲輕舉，深入長驅，難以為功；

translations.chinese: 今將卷甲輕舉，深入長驅，難以為功；
translations.literal: "Now to roll up armor and move lightly, go deep and drive far, will be hard to turn to merit;"
translations.idiomatic: "To strip for a long raid deep into the steppe is hard to turn into victory;"

context.previous: 夫盛之有衰，猶朝之必莫也。
context.next: 從行則迫脅，衡行則中絕，疾則糧乏，徐則後利，不至千里，人馬乏食。

translations.chinese: 從行則迫脅，衡行則中絕，疾則糧乏，徐則後利，不至千里，人馬乏食。
translations.literal: "if in column then pressed and threatened, if in line then cut in the middle; swift then grain runs short, slow then the enemy gains the advantage; before reaching a thousand li, men and horses lack food."
translations.idiomatic: "march in file and they flank you; march abreast and they sever you; hurry and you outrun your grain; dawdle and they choose the ground; before you cross a thousand li, men and horses starve."

context.previous: 今將卷甲輕舉，深入長驅，難以為功；
context.next: 兵法曰：『遺人獲也。』

translations.chinese: 兵法曰：『遺人獲也。』
translations.literal: "The Art of War says, "You will present the prey to another."'"
translations.idiomatic: "Sunzi warns: you only hand the enemy a gift."

context.previous: 從行則迫脅，衡行則中絕，疾則糧乏，徐則後利，不至千里，人馬乏食。
context.next: 意者有它繆巧可以禽之，則臣不知也；

translations.chinese: 意者有它繆巧可以禽之，則臣不知也；
translations.literal: "If there is some other subtle stratagem by which they can be taken, then your servant does not know it;"
translations.idiomatic: "If you have some secret stratagem I have not heard, say it;"

context.previous: 兵法曰：『遺人獲也。』
context.next: 不然，則未見深入之利也。

translations.chinese: 不然，則未見深入之利也。
translations.literal: "if not, then your servant has not seen the profit in going deep."
translations.idiomatic: "otherwise I see no gain in a deep thrust."

context.previous: 意者有它繆巧可以禽之，則臣不知也；
context.next: 臣故曰『勿擊便』。」

translations.chinese: 臣故曰『勿擊便』。」
translations.literal: "Your servant therefore says, 'Do not strike is advantageous.'"
translations.idiomatic: "So I say: do not strike."

context.previous: 不然，則未見深入之利也。

translations.chinese: 恢曰：「不然。
translations.literal: Hui said, "It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui said again, "Wrong."

context.next: 夫草木遭霜者，不可以風過；

translations.chinese: 夫草木遭霜者，不可以風過；
translations.literal: "Grass and trees that have met frost cannot endure wind passing over them;"
translations.idiomatic: "Frost-bitten grass cannot stand a wind;"

context.previous: 恢曰：「不然。
context.next: 清水明鏡，不可以形逃；

translations.chinese: 清水明鏡，不可以形逃；
translations.literal: "clear water and a bright mirror cannot allow form to escape;"
translations.idiomatic: "clear water and a bright mirror hide nothing;"

context.previous: 夫草木遭霜者，不可以風過；
context.next: 通方之士，不可以文亂。

translations.chinese: 通方之士，不可以文亂。
translations.literal: "a man who comprehends the compass cannot be confused by rhetoric."
translations.idiomatic: "a clear mind is not fooled by words."

context.previous: 清水明鏡，不可以形逃；
context.next: 今臣言擊之者，固非發而深入也，將順因單于之欲，誘而致之邊，吾選梟騎壯士陰伏而處以為之備，審遮險阻以為其戒。

translations.chinese: 今臣言擊之者，固非發而深入也，將順因單于之欲，誘而致之邊，吾選梟騎壯士陰伏而處以為之備，審遮險阻以為其戒。
translations.literal: "Now when your servant speaks of striking, it is indeed not to set out and go deep; we will follow the shanyu's desires, lure and bring him to the border, we will select fierce riders and stalwarts to lie in ambush and wait in readiness, carefully block defiles and passes to serve as his warning."
translations.idiomatic: "When I urge a strike, I do not mean a blind march inland: follow the shanyu's greed, bait him to the wall, hide picked cavalry in the defiles, and seal every pass behind him."

context.previous: 通方之士，不可以文亂。
context.next: 吾勢已定，或營其左，或營其右，或當其前，或絕其後，單于可禽，百全必取。」

translations.chinese: 吾勢已定，或營其左，或營其右，或當其前，或絕其後，單于可禽，百全必取。」
translations.literal: "When our dispositions are fixed, we may camp on his left or camp on his right, or bar his front or cut off his rear—the shanyu can be captured; a hundred plans will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: "Once the net is set—left, right, front, rear—the shanyu can be taken; it is a sure thing."

context.previous: 今臣言擊之者，固非發而深入也，將順因單于之欲，誘而致之邊，吾選梟騎壯士陰伏而處以為之備，審遮險阻以為其戒。

translations.chinese: 上曰：「善。」
translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Agreed."

context.next: 乃從恢議，陰使聶壹為間，亡入匈奴，謂單于曰：「吾能斬馬邑令丞，以城降，財物可盡得。」

translations.chinese: 乃從恢議，陰使聶壹為間，亡入匈奴，謂單于曰：「吾能斬馬邑令丞，以城降，財物可盡得。」
translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Hui's plan, secretly sent Nie Yi as a spy, who fled into the Xiongnu and said to the shanyu, "I can behead the magistrate and assistant of Mayi and surrender the city with it; goods and wealth can all be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: He adopted Wang Hui's plan, sent Nie Yi as a double agent into the Xiongnu, and had him tell the shanyu, "Kill Mayi's magistrate and yield the city—the treasury is yours."

context.previous: 上曰：「善。」
context.next: 單于愛信，以為然而許之。

translations.chinese: 單于愛信，以為然而許之。
translations.literal: The shanyu loved and trusted him, thought it true, and consented.
translations.idiomatic: The shanyu believed him and agreed.

context.previous: 乃從恢議，陰使聶壹為間，亡入匈奴，謂單于曰：「吾能斬馬邑令丞，以城降，財物可盡得。」
context.next: 聶壹乃詐斬死罪囚，縣其頭馬邑城下，視單于使者為信，曰：「馬邑長吏已死，可急來。」

translations.chinese: 聶壹乃詐斬死罪囚，縣其頭馬邑城下，視單于使者為信，曰：「馬邑長吏已死，可急來。」
translations.literal: Nie Yi then falsely beheaded a condemned prisoner, hung his head below the wall of Mayi, showed the shanyu's envoy as proof, and said, "The chief officers of Mayi are already dead; you may come quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Nie Yi executed a criminal, hung the head at Mayi as proof to the shanyu's envoy, and said, "The officials are dead—come at once."

context.previous: 單于愛信，以為然而許之。
context.next: 於是單于穿塞，將十萬騎入武州塞。

translations.chinese: 於是單于穿塞，將十萬騎入武州塞。
translations.literal: Thereupon the shanyu broke through the barrier and led a hundred thousand riders into the Wuzhou barrier.
translations.idiomatic: The shanyu breached the wall and rode a hundred thousand horsemen through Wuzhou pass.

context.previous: 聶壹乃詐斬死罪囚，縣其頭馬邑城下，視單于使者為信，曰：「馬邑長吏已死，可急來。」

translations.chinese: 當是時，漢伏兵車騎材官三十餘萬，匿馬邑旁谷中。
translations.literal: At that time Han had ambushed more than three hundred thousand chariot troops, cavalry, and specialist troops, concealed in the valleys beside Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred thousand Han chariots, horse, and specialist troops lay hidden in the ravines near Mayi.

context.next: 衛尉李廣為驍騎將軍，太僕公孫賀為輕車將軍，大行王恢為將屯將軍，太中大夫李息為材官將軍。

translations.chinese: 衛尉李廣為驍騎將軍，太僕公孫賀為輕車將軍，大行王恢為將屯將軍，太中大夫李息為材官將軍。
translations.literal: Commandant of the guards Li Guang was general of fierce cavalry, Grand Coachman Gongsun He was general of light chariots, Grand Coach Wang Hui was general of encamped troops, Grand Counselor Li Xi was general of specialist troops.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the guards Li Guang led the swift cavalry; grand coachman Gongsun He the light chariots; grand coach Wang Hui the camp army; grand counselor Li Xi the specialist corps.

context.previous: 當是時，漢伏兵車騎材官三十餘萬，匿馬邑旁谷中。
context.next: 御史大夫安國為護軍將軍，諸將皆屬。

translations.chinese: 御史大夫安國為護軍將軍，諸將皆屬。
translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Anguo was general who guards the army; all generals were subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Han Anguo was protector-general; every commander answered to him.

context.previous: 衛尉李廣為驍騎將軍，太僕公孫賀為輕車將軍，大行王恢為將屯將軍，太中大夫李息為材官將軍。
context.next: 約單于入馬邑縱兵。

translations.chinese: 約單于入馬邑縱兵。
translations.literal: They agreed that when the shanyu entered Mayi they would loose the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was to spring the trap once the shanyu entered Mayi.

context.previous: 御史大夫安國為護軍將軍，諸將皆屬。
context.next: 王恢、李息別從代主擊輜重。

translations.chinese: 王恢、李息別從代主擊輜重。
translations.literal: Wang Hui and Li Xi separately followed the Prince of Dai to strike the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui and Li Xi were to swing from Dai against the wagon train.

context.previous: 約單于入馬邑縱兵。
context.next: 於是單于入塞，未至馬邑百餘里，覺之，還去。

translations.chinese: 於是單于入塞，未至馬邑百餘里，覺之，還去。
translations.literal: Thereupon the shanyu entered the barrier; when he had not yet reached Mayi by more than a hundred li, he perceived the ruse and turned back and left.
translations.idiomatic: The shanyu crossed the wall but smelled a trap a hundred li short of Mayi and wheeled away.

context.previous: 王恢、李息別從代主擊輜重。
context.next: 語在《匈奴傳》。

translations.chinese: 語在《匈奴傳》。
translations.literal: The account is in the "Treatise on the Xiongnu."
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the Treatise on the Xiongnu.

context.previous: 於是單于入塞，未至馬邑百餘里，覺之，還去。
context.next: 塞下傳言單于已去，漢兵追至塞，度弗及，王恢等皆罷兵。

translations.chinese: 塞下傳言單于已去，漢兵追至塞，度弗及，王恢等皆罷兵。
translations.literal: Below the barrier word passed that the shanyu had already gone; Han troops pursued to the barrier, judged they could not overtake, and Wang Hui and the rest all stood down their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that the shanyu had gone; Han pursuers halted at the wall, saw they could not catch him, and Wang Hui stood his men down.

context.previous: 語在《匈奴傳》。

translations.chinese: 上怒恢不出擊單于輜重也，恢曰：「始約為入馬邑城，兵與單于接，而臣擊其輜重，可得利。
translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Hui had not gone out to strike the shanyu's baggage train; Hui said, "The original agreement was that he would enter Mayi city, troops would engage the shanyu, and your servant would strike his baggage train—gain could be had."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged that Wang Hui had not attacked the baggage train. Wang Hui said, "The plan was for the shanyu to enter Mayi while the main army pinned him; I was to fall on his wagons."

context.next: 今單于不至而還，臣以三萬人眾不敵，祗取辱。

translations.chinese: 今單于不至而還，臣以三萬人眾不敵，祗取辱。
translations.literal: "Now the shanyu did not arrive but returned; your servant with thirty thousand men could not match the enemy—he would only fetch disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: "He never came; my thirty thousand could not have beaten his host—I would only have shamed the throne."

context.previous: 上怒恢不出擊單于輜重也，恢曰：「始約為入馬邑城，兵與單于接，而臣擊其輜重，可得利。
context.next: 固知還而斬，然完陛下士三萬人。」

translations.chinese: 固知還而斬，然完陛下士三萬人。」
translations.literal: "Your servant knew that returning meant execution, yet he preserved Your Majesty's thirty thousand men intact."
translations.idiomatic: "I knew retreat meant death, but I saved your thirty thousand men."

context.previous: 今單于不至而還，臣以三萬人眾不敵，祗取辱。
context.next: 於是下恢廷尉，廷尉當恢逗橈，當斬。

translations.chinese: 於是下恢廷尉，廷尉當恢逗橈，當斬。
translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Hui down to the commandant of justice; the commandant of justice judged Hui for dilatory and weak conduct, meriting execution.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Hui to the commandant of justice, who convicted him of cowardice in the face of the enemy—a capital crime.

context.previous: 固知還而斬，然完陛下士三萬人。」
context.next: 恢行千金丞相蚡，蚡不敢言上，而言於太后曰：「王恢首為馬邑事，今不成而硃恢，是為匈奴報仇也。」

translations.chinese: 恢行千金丞相蚡，蚡不敢言上，而言於太后曰：「王恢首為馬邑事，今不成而硃恢，是為匈奴報仇也。」
translations.literal: Hui carried a thousand in gold weight to Chancellor Fen; Fen did not dare speak to the emperor, but spoke to the empress dowager, saying, "Wang Hui was first to propose the Mayi affair; now that it has failed and they would execute Hui, this is to avenge the Xiongnu."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui bribed Chancellor Tian Fen with a thousand catties of gold; Tian Fen dared not plead to the emperor but told the empress dowager, "Wang Hui began the Mayi plot; to execute him now is to do the Xiongnu a favor."

context.previous: 於是下恢廷尉，廷尉當恢逗橈，當斬。
context.next: 上朝太后，太后以蚡言告上。

translations.chinese: 上朝太后，太后以蚡言告上。
translations.literal: The emperor attended court with the empress dowager; the empress dowager told the emperor Fen's words.
translations.idiomatic: At court with his mother, the emperor heard her repeat Tian Fen's plea.

context.previous: 恢行千金丞相蚡，蚡不敢言上，而言於太后曰：「王恢首為馬邑事，今不成而硃恢，是為匈奴報仇也。」
context.next: 上曰：「首為馬邑事者恢，故發天下兵數十萬，從其言，為此。

translations.chinese: 上曰：「首為馬邑事者恢，故發天下兵數十萬，從其言，為此。
translations.literal: The emperor said, "The one who first proposed the Mayi affair was Hui; therefore I raised several hundred thousand troops of the realm and followed his word in doing this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Hui started Mayi; I mobilized hundreds of thousands on his word."

context.previous: 上朝太后，太后以蚡言告上。
context.next: 且縱單于不可得，恢所部擊，猶頗可得，以尉士大夫心。

translations.chinese: 且縱單于不可得，恢所部擊，猶頗可得，以尉士大夫心。
translations.literal: "Moreover even if the shanyu could not be got, what Hui's command struck could still have been largely got—it would have consoled the hearts of gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: "Even if we missed the shanyu, Wang Hui could still have bloodied the baggage train and heartened the army."

context.previous: 上曰：「首為馬邑事者恢，故發天下兵數十萬，從其言，為此。
context.next: 今不誅恢，無以謝天下。」

translations.chinese: 今不誅恢，無以謝天下。」
translations.literal: "Now if we do not execute Hui, there is no way to apologize to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: "If I spare him, I owe the empire an apology."

context.previous: 且縱單于不可得，恢所部擊，猶頗可得，以尉士大夫心。
context.next: 於是恢聞，乃自殺。

translations.chinese: 於是恢聞，乃自殺。
translations.literal: Thereupon when Hui heard, he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui killed himself when he heard.

translations.chinese: 安國為材官將軍，屯漁陽，捕生口虜，言匈奴遠去。
translations.literal: Anguo was general of specialist troops, encamped at Yuyang, captured living prisoners from the barbarians, who said the Xiongnu had gone far away.
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo, as specialist general at Yuyang, took prisoners who swore the Xiongnu had withdrawn deep into the steppe.

context.next: 即上言方佃作時，請且罷屯。

translations.chinese: 即上言方佃作時，請且罷屯。
translations.literal: He immediately memorialized that it was the season of field work and requested for the nonce to disband the encampment.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that spring planting needed labor and asked to stand the garrison down.

context.previous: 安國為材官將軍，屯漁陽，捕生口虜，言匈奴遠去。
context.next: 罷屯月餘，匈奴大入上谷、漁陽。

translations.chinese: 罷屯月餘，匈奴大入上谷、漁陽。
translations.literal: A month after the encampment was disbanded, the Xiongnu raided in force into Shanggu and Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: A month after he sent the troops home, the Xiongnu smashed into Shanggu and Yuyang.

context.previous: 即上言方佃作時，請且罷屯。
context.next: 安國壁乃有七百餘人，出與戰，安國傷，入壁。

translations.chinese: 安國壁乃有七百餘人，出與戰，安國傷，入壁。
translations.literal: Anguo's rampart then had only more than seven hundred men; he went out to fight; Anguo was wounded and entered the rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Han Anguo had only seven hundred men in his fort; he sortied, was wounded, and crawled back inside.

context.previous: 罷屯月餘，匈奴大入上谷、漁陽。
context.next: 匈奴虜略千餘人及畜產去。

translations.chinese: 匈奴虜略千餘人及畜產去。
translations.literal: The Xiongnu carried off more than a thousand people and livestock and left.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders took over a thousand captives and beasts and rode away.

context.previous: 安國壁乃有七百餘人，出與戰，安國傷，入壁。
context.next: 上怒，使使責讓安國。

translations.chinese: 上怒，使使責讓安國。
translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent envoys to rebuke Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent messengers to blister Han Anguo.

context.previous: 匈奴虜略千餘人及畜產去。
context.next: 徙益東，屯右北平。

translations.chinese: 徙益東，屯右北平。
translations.literal: He was transferred farther east to encamp at Youbeiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted east to garrison Youbeiping.

context.previous: 上怒，使使責讓安國。
context.next: 是時，虜言當入東方。

translations.chinese: 是時，虜言當入東方。
translations.literal: At that time the barbarians said they were about to enter the east.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence said the next strike would fall on the eastern sector.

context.previous: 徙益東，屯右北平。

translations.chinese: 安國始為御史大夫及護軍，後稍下遷。
translations.literal: Anguo had begun as censor-in-chief and protector-general, then was gradually demoted downward.
translations.idiomatic: From censor-in-chief and protector-general he had slid down the ranks.

context.next: 新壯將軍衛青等有功，益貴。

translations.chinese: 新壯將軍衛青等有功，益貴。
translations.literal: The newly favored General Wei Qing and others had merit and grew ever more honored.
translations.idiomatic: Young favorites such as General Wei Qing won glory on the frontier and eclipsed him.

context.previous: 安國始為御史大夫及護軍，後稍下遷。
context.next: 安國既斥疏，將屯又失亡多，甚自愧，幸得罷歸，乃益東徙，意忽忽不樂，數月，病嘔血死。

translations.chinese: 安國既斥疏，將屯又失亡多，甚自愧，幸得罷歸，乃益東徙，意忽忽不樂，數月，病嘔血死。
translations.literal: Anguo, already cast off and estranged, in commanding encampments again lost many to death; he was greatly ashamed, fortunately obtained dismissal to return home, then was moved ever farther east; his mind was depressed and unhappy; after several months he fell ill, vomited blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shunned and stripped of real command, he lost heavily when he tried again to hold a camp; mortified, he begged off, was shunted farther east, sank into gloom, and within months died vomiting blood.

context.previous: 新壯將軍衛青等有功，益貴。

translations.chinese: 壺遂與太史遷等定漢律歷，官至詹事，其人深中篤行君子。
translations.literal: Hu Sui, together with Grand Scribe Sima Qian and others, fixed the Han statutes and calendar; he rose to office as chamberlain for the heir apparent; the man was a gentleman of deep moderation and steadfast conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sui worked with Sima Qian and others on the Han calendar and code, rose to chamberlain for the heir apparent, and was remembered as a grave, steady gentleman.

context.next: 上方倚欲以為相，會其病卒。

translations.chinese: 上方倚欲以為相，會其病卒。
translations.literal: The emperor was leaning on him and wished to make him chancellor, but he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to make him chancellor; he died of illness first.

context.previous: 壺遂與太史遷等定漢律歷，官至詹事，其人深中篤行君子。

translations.chinese: 贊曰：「竇嬰、田蚡皆以外戚重，灌夫用一時決策，而各名顯，並位卿相，大業定矣。
translations.literal: The eulogy says: "Dou Ying and Tian Fen both grew weighty as maternal kin; Guan Fu by a moment's decision of courage—and each made a name, sharing rank as minister and chancellor; the great enterprise was settled."
translations.idiomatic: The historian's judgment: Dou Ying and Tian Fen rose through the empresses' clans; Guan Fu by one rash gesture of courage—all three won fame as ministers, yet the realm had already found its footing.

context.next: 然嬰不知時變，夫亡術而不遜，蚡負貴而驕溢。

translations.chinese: 然嬰不知時變，夫亡術而不遜，蚡負貴而驕溢。
translations.literal: Yet Ying did not know the changes of the times; Fu lacked art and was not deferential; Fen relied on nobility and was arrogant to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Ying misread the age; Guan Fu had no tact; Tian Fen rode his rank into arrogance.

context.previous: 贊曰：「竇嬰、田蚡皆以外戚重，灌夫用一時決策，而各名顯，並位卿相，大業定矣。
context.next: 凶德參會，待時而發，藉福區區其間，惡能救斯敗哉！

translations.chinese: 凶德參會，待時而發，藉福區區其間，惡能救斯敗哉！
translations.literal: When vicious virtue met in conjunction, waiting for the moment to break forth—Jifu, petty between them, how could he save this ruin!"
translations.idiomatic: When such vices collided, even Jifu—small man caught between—could not avert the crash."

context.previous: 然嬰不知時變，夫亡術而不遜，蚡負貴而驕溢。
context.next: 以韓安國之見器，臨其摯而顛墜，陵夷以憂死，遇合有命，悲夫！

translations.chinese: 以韓安國之見器，臨其摯而顛墜，陵夷以憂死，遇合有命，悲夫！
translations.literal: "That Han Anguo was regarded as a vessel of worth, yet at the crisis he toppled and fell, declined by degrees and died in grief—meeting and fit have fate; how sad!"
translations.idiomatic: "Han Anguo was reckoned a statesman of capacity, yet at the pinch he stumbled from favor to exile and died brokenhearted—fortune is fate; how bitter."

context.previous: 凶德參會，待時而發，藉福區區其間，惡能救斯敗哉！
context.next: 若王恢為兵首而受其咎，豈命也乎？

translations.chinese: 若王恢為兵首而受其咎，豈命也乎？
translations.literal: "As for Wang Hui who was first in raising troops yet bore the blame—can that be called fate?"
translations.idiomatic: "And Wang Hui, who first waved the army forward yet paid the price—is that fate, or justice?"

context.previous: 以韓安國之見器，臨其摯而顛墜，陵夷以憂死，遇合有命，悲夫！
